The Roc primary weapon is its ER Medium Laser, a weapon that would be respectable on a light BattleMek and is devastating on a seven-ton ProtoMek. The extended-range variant allows engagement at distances where most ProtoMek opponents cannot effectively return fire, giving the Roc a significant tactical advantage in open terrain. Five jump jets provide one hundred and fifty meters of jumping distance, allowing the Roc to exploit terrain features, clear obstacles, and execute flanking maneuvers that ground-bound opponents cannot counter. The sixty-rated fusion engine delivers fifty-four kilometers per hour cruising speed, adequate for keeping pace with medium-weight formations.

The Roc armor protection of thirty-one points is among the best for first-generation ProtoMeks of its weight class, sufficient to absorb multiple medium weapon hits before structural compromise. As an energy-only design, the base Roc has no ammunition dependency, allowing indefinite combat endurance limited only by pilot fatigue and heat buildup. The Roc only significant limitation is the single-weapon loadout, which means a weapon hit or targeting system malfunction reduces the design to a very expensive paperweight. Despite this vulnerability, the Roc ratio of mobility to firepower and its all-around competence have made it the measuring stick against which other ProtoMek designs are judged.

The Roc is a seven-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as the backbone of the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. Widely regarded as the most successful design to emerge from the program, the Roc combines mobility, armor, and firepower more effectively than any of its siblings, making it suitable for a wide variety of attack and defense missions. Built around an ER Medium Laser and five jump jets, the Roc delivers BattleMek-grade firepower from a platform capable of traversing nearly any terrain. Its balance of capabilities made it the most commonly fielded ProtoMek in the Homeworld Clans by the mid-3060s, forming the core of most mixed ProtoMek formations.

The Roc Z was produced by the Society during the Wars of Reaving at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex, then under Clan Goliath Scorpion control. This variant mounts a Magnetic Clamp System that allows the Roc Z to attach to the exterior of an OmniMek for rapid transport, reflecting the Society asymmetric warfare doctrine of rapid deployment and dispersal. Armed with a Medium Chemical Laser and retaining five jump jets, the Roc Z can be delivered directly to the battlefield by a carrier Mek and immediately begin independent operations. Thirty-two points of armor provide adequate protection. Following the Society destruction, surviving Roc Z production data was seized by the Clans that occupied the Abysmal complex.

The Roc was conceived by Smoke Jaguar scientists as the primary combat ProtoMek in the original lineup, designed to balance all the competing demands of speed, protection, and firepower in a single chassis. Where other designs in the program specialized in reconnaissance, anti-infantry work, or heavy fire support, the Roc was intended to be the generalist, capable of performing adequately in any role. The decision to build it around an ER Medium Laser rather than a missile or ballistic weapon reflected the Jaguar scientists emphasis on reliability and endurance over burst damage potential.

The Roc combat debut during the Battle of Huntress in 3060 validated the design philosophy. In the varied terrain of Huntress, from dense jungle to rocky highlands, the Roc jump jets allowed it to operate effectively everywhere while its ER Medium Laser engaged targets at ranges that kept the fragile ProtoMek frame outside the effective envelope of most small arms. Multiple Points of Rocs were credited with delaying Inner Sphere advances long enough for Jaguar forces to establish secondary defensive positions, their combination of firepower and mobility making them difficult targets to pin down.

Following the Jaguar Annihilation, the Roc became arguably the most sought-after ProtoMek design. Virtually every Clan that acquired ProtoMek technology prioritized Roc production, recognizing it as the most versatile and capable design available. Clan Snow Raven established a major production line at the Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha on Dante, while Clan Wolf began manufacturing Rocs at Csesztreg. Clan Goliath Scorpion continued production at the original Abysmal Manufacturing Complex on Huntress, and several other Clans established smaller production runs at various facilities.

The Roc has inspired more variant configurations than any other first-generation ProtoMek. The Roc 2 mounts a Heavy Medium Laser for increased close-range damage. The Roc 3 trades jump jets for a Medium Pulse Laser and heavier armor. The Roc 4 combines an ECM Suite with an AP Gauss Rifle for electronic warfare capability. The Roc 5 pushes jump capability to seven jets with a Medium Chemical Laser. Each variant reflects a different Clan tactical philosophy applied to the proven Roc chassis.

The Wars of Reaving saw the Society produce the Roc Z variant at the Abysmal Manufacturing Complex, equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System for OmniMek transport and a Medium Chemical Laser. The upheaval of the Reaving disrupted several Roc production lines as Clans were absorbed or destroyed, but the design broad production base ensured continuity. The Roc remains the single most commonly fielded ProtoMek design across the surviving Homeworld Clans, its versatility and proven combat record ensuring that it will remain in production for decades to come.

The base Sprite configuration is built around a quad LRM-5 launcher array, with two launchers in the torso and one in each arm, fed by a deep forty-eight-round shared ammunition supply. This provides twelve full salvos of twenty missiles each, a volume of fire that can suppress and destroy targets at ranges normally associated with dedicated missile BattleMeks. Five extended jump jets provide one hundred fifty meters of leaping distance, remarkable for a fifteen-ton design and essential for tactical repositioning given the modest thirty-two kilometers per hour ground speed.

Sixty-five points of armor make the Sprite one of the most heavily protected ProtoMeks in existence, capable of absorbing punishment that would destroy lighter designs several times over. The extended jump jets add to the cost and complexity but provide the terrain mobility needed to prevent the heavy, slow-moving Sprite from being cornered and overwhelmed. Commanders deploy Sprite Points as heavy fire support elements, using their massed LRM barrages to suppress enemy formations at range while faster assets maneuver for flanking positions. The ammunition supply, while generous by ProtoMek standards, remains the design's primary limitation in extended engagements.

The Sprite is a fifteen-ton ultraheavy ProtoMek, the heaviest design in the entire ProtoMek weight class. Developed during the Wars of Reaving, the Sprite pushes ProtoMek technology to its absolute limits, mounting weapons and armor loads that rival light BattleMeks. The design exists at the theoretical maximum of what the ProtoMek cockpit and pilot interface can control, and its sheer mass requires careful tactical employment to compensate for the relatively slow ground speed that results from pushing so much tonnage through a ProtoMek-scale power plant. Despite these limitations, the Sprite provides devastating firepower in a package that costs a fraction of the resources needed for a comparable BattleMek.

The Sprite 2 replaces the quad LRM array with a single torso-mounted ER Large Laser, the most powerful energy weapon ever fitted to a ProtoMek chassis. Three standard jump jets provide ninety meters of leaping distance, reduced from the base model's one hundred fifty. Armor increases marginally to sixty-six points. The ER Large Laser delivers devastating single-shot damage at extreme range with unlimited ammunition endurance, making the Sprite 2 ideal for extended operations where resupply is impossible. However, the variant sacrifices the base model's volume of fire for concentrated single-target damage, requiring different tactical employment. Heat management limits sustained fire rates, as the massive laser generates significant thermal output.

The Sprite represents the culmination of the ultraheavy ProtoMek development programs initiated during the Wars of Reaving. At fifteen tons, it pushes against the theoretical maximum weight that ProtoMek technology can support, and its development required solutions to engineering challenges that had never been encountered at this scale. The pilot interface systems had to be extensively modified to manage the increased complexity, and the cockpit was expanded to accommodate the additional control requirements.

The base Sprite was designed as a dedicated long-range fire support platform, with its quad LRM-5 array providing a volume of missile fire previously achievable only by dedicated missile carriers. The extended jump jets were incorporated after initial testing revealed that the design's slow ground speed left it dangerously vulnerable to flanking maneuvers, and the added mobility transformed the Sprite from a static firebase into a mobile fire support platform capable of repositioning between volleys.

Two additional variants were developed to address different tactical requirements. The Sprite 2 replaced the LRM array with a single ER Large Laser, the most powerful energy weapon ever mounted on a ProtoMek, while reducing jump jets to three standard units. This variant provides devastating single-shot damage output with unlimited ammunition endurance but sacrifices the volume of fire and extended jump capability of the base model. The Sprite 3 took yet another approach, mounting dual Fusillade rapid-fire systems in the torso alongside arm-mounted Medium Chemical Lasers, with five extended jump jets matching the base model. This configuration excels in close-range engagements against mixed formations, combining suppressive fire from the Fusillades with energy damage from the Chemical Lasers. All three variants continue to serve in Homeworld Clan forces, with each filling a distinct tactical niche in the heavy fire support role.

The Minotaur twin ER Medium Lasers give it the most potent energy weapon suite of any first-generation ProtoMek, delivering a combined damage output that can threaten medium-weight BattleMeks at respectable range. As energy-only armament, the weapons have no ammunition dependency, allowing the Minotaur to fight indefinitely without resupply. Three jump jets provide ninety meters of jumping distance, partially compensating for the design slow thirty-two-kilometer-per-hour cruising speed. Thirty-six points of armor make the Minotaur the most heavily protected first-generation ProtoMek, capable of surviving hits that would destroy lighter designs outright.

The Minotaur primary weakness is its glacial ground speed. At thirty-two kilometers per hour, it is easily outpaced by virtually every combat unit on the battlefield, including most assault-class BattleMeks. The jump jets help somewhat, but ninety meters of leaping distance is barely adequate for clearing terrain obstacles. An entire Point of Minotaurs working together can concentrate enough firepower to rapidly destroy light and medium targets, but getting into effective range against mobile opponents requires careful positioning and terrain exploitation. The design is at its best in defensive operations where it can select strong positions and force enemies to come to it, leveraging its firepower and armor from prepared fighting positions.

The Minotaur is a nine-ton first-generation ProtoMek developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar as the heaviest and most powerful design in the original ProtoMek program on Huntress. Built to serve as the assault element of ProtoMek formations, the Minotaur sacrifices speed for devastating firepower and thick armor protection, mounting two ER Medium Lasers that deliver as much damage as many light BattleMeks. Combined with thirty-six points of armor sufficient to withstand a heavy autocannon hit, the Minotaur represented the upper limit of what first-generation ProtoMek technology could achieve. Its intended role as a defensive strongpoint leverages its impressive combat power while minimizing the impact of its slow ground speed.

The experimental Minotaur XP was developed under Clan Star Adder oversight as a maximum-protection close-combat variant. Mounting dual Improved Heavy Small Lasers alongside an SRM-5 launcher, the XP delivers devastating short-range firepower from behind forty-five points of armor. The SRM-5 provides the heaviest single missile salvo available on a ProtoMek chassis. Jump jets and the Magnetic Clamp System are both absent, leaving the XP dependent on its slow ground speed to reach engagement range. This experimental variant demonstrated the potential of improved weapon technology on the heavy ProtoMek platform.

The Minotaur was developed as the capstone of the original Smoke Jaguar ProtoMek program, representing the maximum weight and combat power that first-generation ProtoMek technology could support. Jaguar scientists designed it specifically for the defensive role, recognizing that the ProtoMek concept was best suited to creating multiple small, lethal defensive positions rather than attempting to match BattleMeks in open maneuver warfare. The decision to mount two ER Medium Lasers was considered ambitious for the weight class, but testing proved that the nine-ton chassis could handle the thermal load with proper heat sink integration.

During the Battle of Huntress in 3060, Minotaur Points served as the backbone of Jaguar defensive positions around key installations. Their ability to absorb significant punishment while delivering devastating return fire made them the most feared ProtoMek design among Task Force Serpent personnel. Several Inner Sphere light Mek pilots reported being caught by surprise when what appeared to be a trivially small target returned fire with medium laser energy that could penetrate their armor in two or three exchanges. The Minotaur combination of small size and BattleMek-grade firepower represented a genuinely new tactical challenge.

After the Jaguar Annihilation, the Minotaur became one of the most widely produced ProtoMek designs. Clan Wolf established an early production line at Csesztreg Industriplex Epsilon, while Clan Hell Horses produced Minotaurs at Industriplex Upsilon on Niles. The design straightforward combat philosophy appealed to Clans across the political spectrum, from the aggressive Blood Spirits to the more cautious Diamond Sharks. The Minotaur lack of specialized equipment meant it could be manufactured more easily than probe or ECM-equipped designs.

The Minotaur has inspired the broadest range of variants of any first-generation ProtoMek, reflecting the diverse tactical philosophies of its many operators. The Minotaur 2 mounts an LB-X AC/2 for long-range cluster fire. The Minotaur 3 carries an LRM-12 with jump jets and a faster engine for mobile fire support. The Minotaur 4 mounts a ProtoMek AC/2 with enhanced mobility. The Minotaur P2, from Clan Goliath Scorpion, adds a Magnetic Clamp System with dual Improved Heavy Small Lasers and an SRM-4. The experimental Minotaur XP pushes the armor to forty-five points with Improved Heavy Small Lasers and an SRM-5.

The Wars of Reaving produced the Minotaur Z variant, equipped with a Magnetic Clamp System and an Improved Medium Heavy Laser for Society asymmetric operations. The destruction and restructuring of multiple Clans during the Reaving disrupted production at several facilities, but the Minotaur manufacturing base was broad enough to survive the upheaval. The design remains the standard heavy ProtoMek across the surviving Homeworld Clans, its combination of firepower and protection still unmatched in the first-generation weight range.

The Dragonstar PT is a 150-ton civilian spheroid built to basic construction standards, with a fusion engine providing safe thrust of 2.5g and a maximum of 4g. This performance is adequate for intersystem runs but leaves little margin against faster military vessels. The hull carries standard armor, offering modest protection sufficient to deter casual piracy or discourage a boarding attempt, though the vessel is clearly not designed for sustained combat. Crew quarters consist of Steerage Compartments throughout, reflecting the design's budget construction philosophy.

The PT's armament is light but practical for its role. Two Large Lasers cover the nose and aft arcs, while four Medium Lasers are distributed to cover all remaining firing directions. This arrangement can discourage opportunistic attack without transforming the vessel into a true combat platform. The Jump Infantry Bay accommodates forty troopers or an equivalent load of civilian passengers. A small secondary cargo bay handles additional supplies. The overall balance favors capacity and cost over combat effectiveness, and the Dragonstar offers little resistance to a determined military opponent.

The Dragonstar Passenger Transport is the backbone of the Draconis Combine's intersystem transit network, introduced in 2610 by Yakima Enterprises, a division of the Stellar Trek conglomerate. Designed as a low-cost, easy-to-produce spheroid shuttle, the Dragonstar has ferried government officials, DCMS troops, and civilian passengers between planetary surfaces and vessels waiting in orbit or at jump points for centuries. Despite a reputation for mechanical fragility and poor cost-effectiveness for repairs, the design has embedded itself so thoroughly in Combine logistics that most operators display near-fanatical loyalty to the product line. Its enduring commercial success rests not on technical excellence but on availability, affordability, and the cultural weight of its ancestry.

The Dragonstar Assault Transport is assigned to DCA naval formations and ground-attack support elements tasked with delivering battle armor to contested objectives. Its battle armor compartment accommodates twelve squads, making it a practical assault insertion platform for short-range operations within a system. The updated extended-range weapon systems provide improved engagement capability against light escorts and aerospace fighters, giving the AT better survivability than the passenger variant in contested space. The trade-off is a significantly reduced cargo capacity, limiting the AT to assault operations rather than general resupply. It is typically deployed from larger DropShips or from orbital stations during contested system operations rather than operating independently.

The Dragonstar's origins lie in the Dragon's Stars vessels of the early Draconis Combine expansion era. Those older craft served as transports for Combine diplomats and dignitaries, shuttling officials to worlds being drawn into the growing realm. Over time they became symbols of the Dragon's diplomatic reach. When Yakima Enterprises developed the modern Dragonstar design in 2610, the company deliberately preserved the aesthetic lineage of its predecessor. Updated avionics and modernized systems gave the new vessel genuine utility, while the visual connection to the original helped position it as the natural continuation of Combine interstellar culture.

The vessel's commercial model is unusual. Dragonstars are cheap to build and notoriously prone to breakdown, with most transportation firms retiring examples after roughly 1,000 AU of service rather than paying escalating repair costs. Yakima is fully aware of this pattern and has built its business around it, combining heavy government subsidies with an active secondary market in salvaged parts stripped from retired hulls. Those recovered components frequently reappear in newly manufactured vessels, raising questions about quality but doing little to diminish the near-fanatical operator loyalty the design commands.

The vessel's military evolution came in 3059, when the Draconis Combine Admiralty approached Yakima to develop an assault transport variant. The proliferation of battle armor following the Clan Invasion and a renewed emphasis on naval operations revealed a gap in the Combine's assault transport inventory. With minimal changes to the existing platform, including updated weapon systems but retained armor protection and hull layout, Yakima delivered the Dragonstar Assault Transport to DCA installations barely a year later. The AT's rapid development cycle reflected both Yakima's familiarity with the base design and the Combine's characteristic tendency to militarize commercial platforms rather than develop purpose-built military craft from scratch.

The Mówáng is a 100-ton Civilian Aerodyne Small Craft powered by a standard fusion powerplant delivering a safe thrust of 4G and a maximum thrust of 6G, providing adequate performance for intra-system transit between planetary surfaces, orbital stations, and jump points. Fuel capacity supports routine system hops without requiring intermediate resupply. The craft's three-man crew is drawn from the employing noble's personal staff, valued for discretion rather than combat experience.

Passenger accommodations are modest but well-appointed for a vessel of this class. A single first-class stateroom serves the primary passenger, while two steerage-rated cabins accommodate aides or companions. Cargo capacity is limited to five and a half tons, accessed through a single cargo door, which is sufficient for personal effects, gifts, or contraband at the owner's discretion.

Armor protection amounts to just two and a half tons of standard plating, arranged to deflect debris rather than withstand weapons fire. The Mówáng carries no armament whatsoever. These limitations reflect deliberate design choices: military protection would raise costs and attract inspection. The craft's entire defensive strategy rests on appearing unremarkable. Its construction is intentionally within the manufacturing capability of any modestly industrialized world, which is reflected in its price tag of roughly 3.5 million C-bills.

The Mówáng-class Courier is a compact civilian Small Craft conceived during the early First Succession War to serve the personal transport needs of Capellan Confederation nobility. Commissioned by the House of Scions in 2835, the design was built around simplicity, passenger comfort, and low production cost. The House declared an open manufacturing license immediately upon introduction, inviting any world with adequate industrial capacity to build the craft without restriction. That decision spread the Mówáng across dozens of systems within a few generations, making it among the most widely distributed personal spacecraft in the Inner Sphere. Lightly built and unarmed, the vessel relies on its mundane appearance and near-universal familiarity to pass scrutiny wherever it operates.

The Mówáng serves as a personal transport for nobility, senior officials, and wealthy private owners throughout the Capellan Confederation and neighboring states. Most examples operate as intra-system couriers, moving passengers between planetary surfaces, orbital facilities, and jump points. A smaller number serve as discreet transports for valuables or sensitive cargo where the owner wishes to avoid formal shipping channels. The open manufacturing license means the craft can be found in virtually any Capellan duchy or warren, and examples are common enough in neighboring realms that they rarely attract attention during routine transit.

The Mówáng-class Courier emerged in the early years of the First Succession War, when established DropShip service networks grew unreliable and Capellan nobles sought alternatives for private intra-system travel. The House of Scions, the aristocratic body overseeing Capellan nobility, sponsored the design with specific requirements: the craft had to be affordable, simple to build, and comfortable enough for a Diem to use as a personal vehicle. The open manufacturing license declared in 2835 was a deliberate policy choice, intended to maximize production across the Confederation's many worlds rather than concentrate output at a handful of licensed facilities. Within decades, the design had spread throughout the Capellan Confederation and was being produced by local manufacturers on dozens of worlds.

Throughout the Succession Wars the Mówáng occupied a quiet but persistent niche. Capellan Diems used them to travel between worlds in their multi-planetary holdings, convey valuables, and move goods, licit or otherwise, beyond the reach of formal customs networks. Their unremarkable profile meant that military and customs patrols rarely subjected them to serious scrutiny. As the design spread beyond the Confederation, nobles and wealthy merchants in neighboring states acquired them for the same reasons. By the time of the Clan Invasion, the Mówáng had become common enough in Inner Sphere system traffic that a single craft could move through most ports without comment.

That anonymity proved dangerous during the Jihad. In 3073, the Word of Blake acquired a number of Mówáng hulls provided by Kali Liao and modified them as covert assault transports. The conversions stripped out passenger quarters, installed battle armor bays capable of carrying two Level Is of troops, reduced the engine output to free internal volume, increased armor protection to four tons, and fitted an Angel ECM suite. The modified craft were used as clandestine insertion vehicles, exploiting the Mówáng's civilian identity to approach targets aboard passenger DropShips or JumpShips before executing attack runs. Most of these converted hulls were destroyed or captured before the Jihad concluded, but the episode left a residual wariness. Several jurisdictions instituted enhanced inspection requirements for Mówáng-type craft in the early Republic era, and the vessel's reputation as an innocent courier was never fully restored.

The Tigress is built around a nose-mounted PPC and a fifteen-tube Long Range Missile launcher, giving it effective firepower at both energy and ballistic ranges without the complexity of more varied weapon combinations. The LRM rack carries thirty-two salvos, sufficient for an extended patrol without resupply. For close-range engagements, four medium lasers split between the two wing sections provide respectable short-range firepower, though the Tigress is not optimized for brawling against heavier craft at close quarters.

The craft's fusion engine gives it maximum thrust of 3g, adequate for intercept work in the constrained geometry of system patrol operations. Fifteen tons of fuel support patrols of just over eight days at continuous thrust, a practical endurance for asteroid field and jump point picket duties. A seven-ton cargo bay allows the Tigress to carry limited stores for extended independent operations. The design is solid rather than exceptional, reflecting the Concordat's preference for maintainability and cost of ownership over peak performance. The Tigress's primary vulnerability is the absence of any aft-arc weaponry, leaving it exposed to threats that successfully close behind the craft's forward firing arc.

The Tigress Close Patrol Craft was developed by Vandenberg Mechanized Industries shortly after the fall of the Star League, entering service in 2790 as a dedicated system defense platform for the Taurian Concordat. Originally conceived as a DropShip and WarShip escort in the mold of earlier Star League designs, shifting strategic priorities redirected the Tigress toward local patrol duties as the Concordat focused on defending the densely fortified Hyades Cluster against Successor State aggression. The craft's modest size, self-sufficient fuel supply for patrols of up to a week, and manageable crew requirements made it an ideal platform for operations in the asteroid fields and approach corridors of the Cluster. Neither the fastest nor the most heavily armed craft of its type, the Tigress trades raw performance for the reliability, endurance, and affordability that a Periphery power requires from a frontline patrol asset.

The Tigress Close Patrol Craft serves almost exclusively with the Taurian Concordat Aerospace Forces, assigned primarily to defensive patrol duties in the Hyades Cluster. Craft are typically deployed in small groups covering asteroid belts, jump point approaches, and inner system corridors of inhabited worlds. The seven-ton cargo bay allows Tigress patrols to carry limited supplies for extended independent operations, reducing resupply frequency in the Concordat's resource-constrained Periphery environment. A small number of Tigress craft have reached the hands of Periphery operators and independent actors over the centuries, though the design's Taurian-specific support infrastructure has limited its spread beyond Concordat space.

Vandenberg Mechanized Industries began designing the Tigress as the Aquarius and Lyonesse were disappearing from production. The escort small craft role those designs had built was contracting across the Inner Sphere, absorbed by heavier aerospace fighters and newer DropShip classes. Vandenberg's designers looked at that contraction and reached a different conclusion than the major powers had. For the Taurian Concordat, with its densely fortified Hyades Cluster and its permanent concern about Federated Suns aggression, the need for affordable, self-sufficient patrol craft had not diminished. It had grown. The Tigress, introduced in 2790, carried that lineage forward into the Periphery while the Inner Sphere abandoned it.

The original design intent was closer to the Aquarius than what the Tigress became. Vandenberg planned a DropShip and WarShip escort operating in the Star League tradition. Shifting strategic priorities during development redirected the craft toward system patrol duties, covering the asteroid fields and approach corridors of the Hyades Cluster rather than riding alongside capital ships. The PPC and LRM armament suited this role well, engaging threats at range before they could threaten defended installations or passing convoys. For nearly three centuries the Tigress served that function with little change, operated by minimal crews on week-long patrols through some of the most heavily mined and monitored space in the Periphery.

The design earned wider recognition during the Jihad. In 3076, Taurian gunships participated in a nuclear strike raid on the New Syrtis Shipyards, a suicidal deployment that crippled the facility and underscored both the Concordat's willingness to commit its patrol craft offensively and the depth of political tensions that had been building with the Federated Suns. Vandenberg continued production through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, making the Tigress one of the longest-lived small craft designs of the Periphery, an unbroken line of service that outlasted the Inner Sphere powers that had abandoned the escort role entirely.

The Foxhound carries a potent mix of advanced weapons for a craft of its size. Two extended-range large lasers provide reliable long-range fire from the nose, with Improved Targeting hardware enhancing their effective reach. The craft's most powerful weapons are a pair of improved heavy Gauss rifles mounted on its sides, capable of delivering punishing firepower against larger vessels and fortified positions alike. Laser anti-missile systems protect both the nose and aft arcs, giving the crew meaningful defense against incoming missile salvos.

The Foxhound carries 16.5 tons of heavy ferro-aluminum armor, providing solid protection relative to its 180-ton frame. Twenty double heat sinks manage the thermal load from the laser battery, though coolant feeds have proven vulnerable to bursting under sustained fire. That heat management problem, combined with Non-Standard Parts sourced through the Word of Blake technology exchange, makes the craft difficult and costly to maintain in the field. The Hard to Pilot designation reflects demanding handling characteristics that strain smaller crews across extended engagements. The lighter fuel load further limits independent endurance, making the Foxhound dependent on fixed bases or tender support for anything beyond short-duration sorties.

The TiG-40 Foxhound is a military spheroid Small Craft designed and produced by Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on New Vandenberg for the Taurian Defense Force. Introduced in 3083, the Foxhound was conceived as a defensive gunboat to replace combat losses suffered during the Jihad-era fighting near Taurian space. Development relied on advanced technology acquired through a brief exchange with the Word of Blake, giving the craft weapons and systems far beyond typical Concordat production standards. The name itself reflects a pointed cultural statement: named deliberately to evoke the Federated Suns and its celebrated leader, the designation expressed the contempt many within the Concordat felt toward their longtime rival. First deployed in the Hyades Cluster, the Foxhound represented a bold step in the Concordat's effort to reconstitute and modernize the TDF following the Jihad.

The TiG-40 serves exclusively within the Taurian Concordat's border defense networks, concentrated primarily in the Hyades Cluster. Its role is interception and deterrence, challenging vessels entering Concordat space without authorization and providing heavier firepower than the older Tigress in engagements where a harder punch is required. A crew of four manages all shipboard functions, reflecting the Foxhound's lean design philosophy. Maintenance demands pose a persistent operational challenge in forward-deployed settings, where Non-Standard Parts sourced through the Word of Blake exchange are difficult to procure through conventional supply channels. The Foxhound performs best when operating from a fixed facility or tender vessel, and is not suited for extended independent operations away from support infrastructure.

The Foxhound's origins lie in the Taurian Concordat's wartime losses and its complicated relationship with the Word of Blake during the Jihad. The TDF suffered significant losses among its TiG-15 gunboats during fighting near Federated Suns systems, leaving a gap in the Concordat's border defense capacity. When the opportunity arose to acquire advanced technology through an exchange with the Word of Blake, Vandenberg Mechanized Industries moved quickly to incorporate those systems into a new design.

The decision to accept Blakist technical assistance reflected the broader posture of the Concordat's military leadership during that period. The junta pursued its hostility toward the Federated Suns with single-minded focus, and the Blakist connection provided both weapons technology and a means to strike at a rival. Even as Blakist forces conducted devastating attacks on Federated Suns civilian populations, Concordat leadership framed those events through the lens of its own grievances, dismissing evidence that complicated its preferred narrative. The resulting craft bore a name chosen to antagonize: the Foxhound, a deliberate invocation of the Federated Suns and the contempt with which many Taurians regarded them.

The first Foxhounds entered service in the Hyades Cluster in the mid-3080s, joining the Tigress gunboats already stationed there on patrol duty. The two designs complemented each other in theory, with the Foxhound providing heavier firepower to offset the Tigress's longer patrol endurance. In practice, Non-Standard Parts and demanding maintenance requirements limited operational availability from the outset, a problem that the TDF struggled to address through subsequent decades of service. Despite those challenges, the Foxhound remained a fixture of Taurian border defense through the ilClan era, valued for its firepower even if its logistical footprint remained a persistent frustration for maintenance crews.

The Mk.III Assault Craft substantially upgrades both propulsion and protection over the base Ares design. Its more powerful primitive fusion engine nearly doubles the maximum thrust of the Mk.I, allowing the craft to pursue and intercept enemy fighters rather than simply defend. Heavier armor and additional heat sinks reflect the shift to a direct combat role.

The Mark VII carries six medium lasers across the nose, wings, and aft positions, supplemented by two nose-mounted small lasers. A Fusion 200 engine provides safe thrust 4 and maximum thrust 6. Thirteen tons of standard armor protect the hull, with nose concentration. A 31-ton cargo bay is retained alongside the weapons systems. The Mark VII's VTOL hover capability allows it to land in rough terrain without prepared strips, an advantage over conventional aerodyne designs that require prepared surfaces. The design's reliance on short-range energy weapons makes it most effective in close engagements, and it performs poorly against opponents who can maintain standoff range.

The Mark VII-C substitutes Clan medium pulse lasers for IS medium lasers and fits Clan double heat sinks, improving thermal efficiency while retaining the same combat silhouette. Clan standard armor runs one ton lighter than the IS version but provides superior protection values.

The Ares Assault Craft represents the combat-hardened branch of the Ares small craft lineage, tracing its origins to the primitive Mk.III of 2451 and evolving into the Mark VII, one of the most widely produced military landing craft in the Inner Sphere. Developed by IncStar Dynamics as a dedicated fighter-engagement variant, the Mk.III prioritized combat capability while retaining limited cargo capacity. Its heavier engine and upgraded armor set a template that later designers refined during the Succession Wars into the standard-technology Mark VII, produced at multiple factories and fielded by every major Inner Sphere power. The Clan adaptation, designated the Mark VII-C, brought advanced Clan technology to the same proven airframe, completing the long evolution from a primitive Age of War design into a craft that would serve in front-line roles across the entire Inner Sphere and Clan space well into the ilClan era.

The Mark VII-C fills the same orbit-to-surface transport role in Clan service as the IS variant does in the Inner Sphere, and the two designs are operationally interchangeable for most purposes. Clan Ghost Bear operated it from their Tseng Facility in orbit around Alshain, assigning the design to transport wings supporting planetary assault operations in their occupation zone. Clan Jade Falcon added production at the Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten from 3074, integrating the Mark VII-C into Jade Falcon assault doctrine across the occupation zone. The upgraded pulse laser armament and double heat sink efficiency give the Mark VII-C a meaningful edge over the IS variant in close-range engagements, though for pure cargo delivery the practical differences are minimal. Both IS and Clan versions appear regularly in salvage and black market circulation across the Inner Sphere and Clan space.

IncStar Dynamics introduced the Mk.III Assault Craft in 2451 as the third branch of the original Ares family, joining the Mk.I long-range landing craft and the Mk.II close attack landing craft on the same base hull. Where the Mk.I carried cargo and the Mk.II provided escort suppression, the Mk.III was built for direct fighter engagement. Its more powerful engine gave it the thrust to pursue and intercept, and reinforced armor allowed it to absorb damage that would have disabled the other marks. All three designs operated together in HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period, each branch complementing the others on contested planetary approaches.

The fall of the Star League and the Succession Wars stripped away the manufacturing base that supported the original Ares family. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War, having already dropped the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward. By 2824, a simplified but robust successor emerged: the Mark VII, the standard-technology heir to the Mk.I long-range landing craft branch. Produced at factories across the Successor States and the Taurian Concordat, the Mark VII carried the landing craft lineage forward while the close attack branch of the Mk.II was absorbed into broader doctrine and the assault craft branch of the Mk.III lay dormant.

The Mark VII-C emerged in 2841 with Clan technology. Clan Ghost Bear produced it at their Tseng Facility in orbit around Alshain, and Clan Jade Falcon added production at the Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten in 3074. Both the IS Mark VII and the Clan Mark VII-C share the introduction year of 2841 despite the decades of isolation between the two civilizations, leading historians to conclude that both designs evolved independently from a shared earlier ancestor rather than one copying the other.

The assault craft branch of the family did not stay dormant permanently. Universal Air maintained the original Ares design archives through the Succession Wars and the Clan Invasion era. After merging with Federated Boeing, the company restarted Ares attack craft production in 3066 and introduced the Mark IX in 3077, completing the revival of the third branch and reuniting all three lines of the original Ares family under active production for the first time since the Star League era.

The S-7A is built around three separable modules linked by explosive bolts: a forward passenger section accommodating ten occupants and a pilot, a central cargo section with two pressurized bays totaling 31.5 tons of capacity, and an aft engineering module housing the fusion drive. The modular architecture allows any single section to be jettisoned in an emergency, with a surrounding framework ensuring the remaining two sections stay functional. The secondary cargo bay maintains independent pressurization, serving as an airlock for the main hold.

With a safe thrust of 3G and no weapons, the Bus prioritizes capacity and reliability over performance. It depends entirely on its host vessel or installation for any defensive capability, making independent operation outside protected environments impractical.

The S-7A Bus is a civilian aerodyne Small Craft produced by Shipil Company of Skye beginning in 2602, designed for personnel and cargo transport in the vacuum of space. Its non-aerodynamic hull prevents atmospheric operations, but this limitation was accepted in exchange for greater cargo volume than comparable aerodyne designs. The type became one of the most widely distributed Small Craft in the Inner Sphere, serving a broad range of operators across multiple states.

The S-7AC fills the same logistical role as the S-7A but aboard Clan vessels and installations. Production was established at Clan-controlled orbital facilities, and the S-7AC became a standard Small Craft complement for WarShip crews across multiple Clans.

Shipil Company introduced the S-7A Bus in 2602, and broad licensing during the Star League era spread production to manufacturers across the Inner Sphere, including Earthwerks Ltd. in the Capellan Confederation, Tomori Trans Industrial in the Draconis Combine, and Vandenberg Mechanized Industries in the Taurian Concordat. This wide distribution gave the design remarkable survivability through the Succession Wars, with multiple independent production lines maintaining output despite conflict and industrial disruption.

Clan forces adapted the platform in 2843, producing the S-7AC variant with Clan-specification armor for use aboard their WarShips and orbital installations. Both Inner Sphere and Clan versions remained in active production into the Dark Age period.

The K-1 is built around a Pratt & Whitney 400 fusion engine, providing a safe thrust of 4 and a maximum of 6, adequate for standard orbital operations and short transit runs. The spheroid hull carries 21 tons of standard armor distributed with a deliberate emphasis on the nose, where protection is more than twice as thick as on the flanks or aft. This arrangement reflects the craft's typical approach orientation and the expectation that threats will most often come from ahead. Heat management is handled by ten single heat sinks, which are sufficient for the limited weapons array the K-1 mounts.

For defense, the K-1 carries a light but practical armament: an LRM-5 launcher and a medium laser covering the nose, a medium laser on each broadside, and a medium laser paired with a small laser pointing aft. This provides coverage across all facings without dedicating the craft to a combat role it was never intended to fill. The LRM-5 gives the crew some standoff capability, though ammunition is limited to 48 rounds. Range and endurance rather than firepower define the K-1's design philosophy.

The crew compartment accommodates a single officer and three enlisted ratings, and Sarna sources note the cockpit is especially cramped, with only three seats. Six passengers travel in steerage, and the cargo bay holds sixteen and a half tons, modest compared to full DropShips but well suited to the supply runs and personnel transfers the K-1 was built to handle. The docking collar, unusual for a Small Craft, allows the K-1 to ride a JumpShip hardpoint between systems, though the economics of reserving a hardpoint for a 200-ton vessel grew increasingly difficult to justify as JumpShips became scarce after the Star League's fall.

The K-1 DropShuttle is a 200-ton spheroid Small Craft developed by Earthwerks Incorporated and introduced in 2536, during the height of Star League prosperity when JumpShip passage was routine and inexpensive. The K-1 holds the distinction of being the smallest space vehicle equipped with a docking collar, allowing it to attach to a JumpShip hardpoint in the manner of a conventional DropShip despite its Small Craft classification. Designed to carry modest cargo and a handful of passengers on short interstellar hops, the K-1 filled the niche between the purely atmospheric shuttle and the full-sized DropShip. Earthwerks licensed the design broadly during the Star League era, and production lines appeared across nearly every major member state. The Clans preserved both the design and its original operational doctrine well into the ilClan era.

The K-1 serves throughout the Inner Sphere in a general-purpose shuttle role, moving small cargo consignments and passengers between orbital facilities, planetary surfaces, and JumpShip jump points. It is most commonly found in the retinue of merchant JumpShips and exploration vessels, where its modest size suits operations in cramped docking facilities. Military units sometimes operate K-1s as utility craft for resupply runs or officer transport when a full DropShip would be impractical. Parts availability is generally good throughout the Inner Sphere given the breadth of historical production.

The K-1 DropShuttle traces its origins to Earthwerks Incorporated's production lines on Terra, where the design entered service in 2536. At that time, JumpShip access was routine and the cost of interstellar passage remained within reach of civilian travelers and small commercial concerns. Earthwerks recognized a market for a small, economical craft capable of attaching directly to a JumpShip hardpoint while remaining small enough to manage without a dedicated DropShip berth. The resulting design was licensed broadly, with manufacturers across the Terran Hegemony, Capellan Confederation, Federated Suns, Free Worlds League, Lyran Commonwealth, and Draconis Combine all running production lines at various points during the Star League era.

The collapse of the Star League and the devastation of the Succession Wars reshaped the K-1's role fundamentally. With JumpShips becoming scarce and interstellar passage increasingly expensive, the economics of booking an entire hardpoint for a 200-ton Small Craft no longer made sense for most operators. The K-1 drifted into the general long-range shuttle role, competing on cargo and passenger capacity with vessels like the KR-61. The craft remained viable in this reduced capacity thanks to its widespread manufacture and the ready availability of spare parts. Most operators found that while the K-1 could no longer justify its unique docking collar feature economically, the vessel itself remained practical and cost-effective for in-system work.

The Clans, who preserved many Star League technologies and operational doctrines, continued operating the K-1 in its original role. Clan technicians introduced the K-1C variant in 2914, upgrading the weapons and armor to Clan specifications while retaining the fundamental design. Clan Jade Falcon restarted dedicated K-1C production at their Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten in 3074, and Clan Ghost Bear maintained a production line at the Tseng Facility on Alshain, later passing to the Rasalhague Dominion. In the Inner Sphere, Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on Illiushin kept the Taurian Concordat supplied throughout the entire period from Star League to ilClan, and the United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora, later operating under Raven Alliance control, resumed production in the Dark Age. The Draconis Combine, Capellan Confederation, and Free Worlds League all sustained their own production lines, ensuring the K-1 remained in active service more than six centuries after its introduction.

The KR-61's primary distinction over the shorter-ranged ST-46 is its extended endurance. Carrying double the fuel of that companion design, it can complete round trips to zenith and nadir jump points without refueling stops. A Pitban 300a fusion engine provides propulsion, yielding a safe acceleration of 2G and a maximum of 3G, adequate for civilian in-system transit.

The passenger section includes sleeping, sanitary, and food preparation accommodations for two crew members and two passengers, a level of comfort unusual in small craft of this mass and entirely absent from the ST-46. Six tons of standard armor provides some deterrence against piracy but offers no serious defensive capability, and the KR-61 is entirely unarmed. Its small cargo hold, which also serves as the sole airlock, limits the vessel's utility as a general freighter. The KR-61 Long-Range Shuttlecraft is the most common aerodyne long-range shuttle in use across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Designed in 2598 to fill the gap between the short-range ST-46 Shuttle and full DropShips, the KR-61 carries small numbers of passengers and modest cargo between planets and jump points whenever an attached DropShip cannot be detached from its JumpShip. Manufactured at facilities across every major faction since its Star League-era introduction, the KR-61 became one of the most widely distributed civilian spacecraft in human space, a common fixture at jump points, orbital stations, and civilian spaceports from the Magistracy of Canopus to the Draconis Combine.

The KR-61 serves in virtually every faction across the Inner Sphere and Periphery, operating wherever JumpShips require a dedicated long-range shuttle. It carries passengers, mail, and light cargo consignments between planets and jump points, and is a common sight aboard JumpShips and at orbital facilities throughout known space.

The ST-46 entered service first, in 2528, establishing a broad production base among the major Houses as the standard workhorse shuttle for JumpShips, WarShips, space stations, and large transport vessels. The KR-61 followed seventy years later, in 2598, purpose-built to address the ST-46's primary limitation: with only 5 tons of fuel, the ST-46 could not reliably service the long distances between inner system worlds and zenith or nadir jump points. The KR-61's doubled fuel capacity and extended habitability accommodations filled that gap, and the two designs have operated in complementary roles ever since.

Many of the same manufacturing facilities produce both types. Earthwerks Ltd. on Ares maintained uninterrupted Capellan production of both shuttles across every era from the Star League through the ilClan period. Hinsdale Elec on Dover did the same for the Draconis Combine. Andurien AeroTech operated lines for both at Lopez and Westover in Free Worlds League space. The United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora produced both designs for the Outworlds Alliance and later the Raven Alliance. This shared production base helped ensure both types survived the technological regression of the Succession Wars, remaining available across all major factions even as more complex spacecraft fell out of production.

Additional producers served individual factions. Semier Data Tron on Tharkad supplied the Lyran Commonwealth with ST-46s from the Star League through the Civil War era before shutting down during the Jihad. Shipil Company on Skye and Majesty Metals and Manufacturing on Dunianshire each produced the KR-61 without a corresponding ST-46 line. Federated-Boeing Interstellar at Port Simon Shipyards on Galax produced both for the Federated Suns and later the Federated Commonwealth.

Clan versions of both designs emerged centuries into the Succession Wars period. The ST-46C appeared in 2897, initially misidentified by some Inner Sphere observers as captured IS craft given its unarmed civilian configuration. The KR-61C followed in 2851, adopting Clan-grade composite armor for a modest improvement in protection. Full Clan Occupation Zone production of both Clan variants began by 3080, with Clan Jade Falcon's Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten and the Ghost Bear Tseng Facility on Alshain manufacturing both the ST-46C and KR-61C alongside one another, maintaining the paired production pattern established by their Inner Sphere predecessors.

The Battle Taxi relies on a safe thrust of three gravities, with a maximum acceleration of four and a half gravities, to close rapidly with target vessels during boarding actions. A pair of magnetic grapples and a hull-mounted tug adapter allow the craft to latch onto enemy DropShips, JumpShips, or even WarShips, pulling itself alongside to disgorge its marine contingent. If the tug adapter cannot achieve a proper seal, embarked marines can use magnetic boots and cutting tools to create alternate access points along the target hull.

Armament consists of paired extended-range large lasers mounted in the wing sections for long-range suppressive fire during approach, supplemented by four medium pulse lasers split between the wings for close-range defense. Thirty-two tons of standard armor provide substantial protection during the vulnerable approach phase. The craft's cargo hold accommodates fifty tons of personnel and equipment, typically two points of battle armor or three full platoons of conventional infantry. A crew of three operates the vessel, though a single pilot can manage the craft at reduced effectiveness if necessary.

The NL-42 Battle Taxi is a two-hundred-ton boarding transport small craft originally designed by Blackwell Corporation on New Valencia. Introduced in 3053 as the military equivalent of the ubiquitous S-7A shuttle bus, the Battle Taxi was purpose-built for ship-to-ship boarding operations against DropShips, JumpShips, and WarShips. Its combination of speed, heavy armor protection, and generous troop capacity made it an immediate success with naval forces across the Inner Sphere, and the design was quickly licensed to manufacturers in every major Successor State. The craft's straightforward construction and reliable performance earned it a reputation as the standard small craft for marine assault operations, a role it continues to fill decades after its introduction.

The base NL-42 represents the standard production model as manufactured by Blackwell Corporation and its numerous licensees. This configuration has remained essentially unchanged since its introduction, reflecting the proven nature of the design's balance of approach speed, defensive firepower, and troop capacity for conventional ship-to-ship boarding missions across both naval and anti-piracy operations.

The NL-42 emerged from Blackwell Corporation's extensive experience supporting Wolf's Dragoons, who had long relied on boarding operations as part of their combined-arms doctrine. The design drew on Star League-era boarding craft concepts, updated with technologies available in the early 3050s. Blackwell's close relationship with the Dragoons meant the craft was field-tested extensively before being offered on the open market, and the Dragoons' own variant, known as the Lupus, became the first operational model.

The design's immediate popularity led to rapid licensing across the Inner Sphere. Andurien AeroTech on Westover, Earthwerks Limited on Ares, Shipil Company on Skye, and Tomori Trans Industrial on Chatham all secured production rights, ensuring that every major Successor State gained access to the craft within a decade of its introduction. This broad manufacturing base reflected growing demand for dedicated boarding craft as naval operations expanded during the Clan Invasion era and the subsequent Civil War period.

The use of extended-range and pulse laser technology in the base design created a historical curiosity. Sarna records suggest the NL-42 class saw service during earlier, lower-technology eras of the Succession Wars, when such advanced weapon systems were unavailable. What weapons the earlier models carried remains undocumented, though the Lupus variant used by Wolf's Dragoons is confirmed to have mounted the full advanced weapons suite. The Jihad disrupted several production lines, especially Blackwell's facility on New Valencia, but the distributed manufacturing network ensured the Battle Taxi remained available throughout the conflict and into the post-Jihad era. Production continues at multiple sites across the Inner Sphere, with ownership changes reflecting the political upheavals of the Dark Age and ilClan periods.

The S-7A is built around three separable modules linked by explosive bolts: a forward passenger section accommodating ten occupants and a pilot, a central cargo section with two pressurized bays totaling 31.5 tons of capacity, and an aft engineering module housing the fusion drive. The modular architecture allows any single section to be jettisoned in an emergency, with a surrounding framework ensuring the remaining two sections stay functional. The secondary cargo bay maintains independent pressurization, serving as an airlock for the main hold.

With a safe thrust of 3G and no weapons, the Bus prioritizes capacity and reliability over performance. It depends entirely on its host vessel or installation for any defensive capability, making independent operation outside protected environments impractical.

The S-7A Bus is a civilian aerodyne Small Craft produced by Shipil Company of Skye beginning in 2602, designed for personnel and cargo transport in the vacuum of space. Its non-aerodynamic hull prevents atmospheric operations, but this limitation was accepted in exchange for greater cargo volume than comparable aerodyne designs. The type became one of the most widely distributed Small Craft in the Inner Sphere, serving a broad range of operators across multiple states.

The S-7A serves as a utility transport aboard JumpShips, DropShips, and orbital installations throughout the Inner Sphere. Its unarmed, space-only configuration limits it to non-combat support roles, but for routine personnel transfer and cargo handling it is reliable and easy to maintain.

Shipil Company introduced the S-7A Bus in 2602, and broad licensing during the Star League era spread production to manufacturers across the Inner Sphere, including Earthwerks Ltd. in the Capellan Confederation, Tomori Trans Industrial in the Draconis Combine, and Vandenberg Mechanized Industries in the Taurian Concordat. This wide distribution gave the design remarkable survivability through the Succession Wars, with multiple independent production lines maintaining output despite conflict and industrial disruption.

Clan forces adapted the platform in 2843, producing the S-7AC variant with Clan-specification armor for use aboard their WarShips and orbital installations. Both Inner Sphere and Clan versions remained in active production into the Dark Age period.

The craft carries 18.5 tons of standard armor, substantially more protection than the KR-61's 6 tons, reflecting its more frequent atmospheric and docking operations where minor collisions and landing stress are routine. Passenger capacity is eight, accessed through the cockpit or the vessel's single airlock. The 12-ton cargo hold offers nearly five times the payload of the KR-61, reinforcing the ST-46's role as a bulk short-range workhorse rather than a long-haul passenger craft.

Introduced in 2528, seventy years before the more specialized KR-61 Long-Range Shuttlecraft, the ST-46 became the standard short-hop utility craft for JumpShips, WarShips, space stations, and large transports throughout known space. Designed for reliability and versatility over passenger comfort or long-range endurance, it filled a niche no other single vessel could claim as broadly as its own.

The ST-46C performs the same role within Clan Occupation Zones, serving Jade Falcon and Ghost Bear logistics networks. Its slightly improved Clan-grade composite armor and marginally increased cargo capacity provide a modest performance edge over the Inner Sphere variant, though the fundamental operational profile is identical.

The ST-46 Shuttle and KR-61 Long-Range Shuttlecraft together form the backbone of civilian small craft logistics across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. The ST-46 entered service first, in 2528, establishing a broad production base among the major Houses as the standard workhorse shuttle for JumpShips, WarShips, space stations, and large transport vessels. The KR-61 followed seventy years later, in 2598, purpose-built to address the ST-46's primary limitation: with only 5 tons of fuel, the ST-46 could not reliably service the long distances between inner system worlds and zenith or nadir jump points. The KR-61's doubled fuel capacity and extended habitability accommodations filled that gap, and the two designs have operated in complementary roles ever since.

Many of the same manufacturing facilities produce both types. Earthwerks Ltd. on Ares maintained uninterrupted Capellan production of both shuttles across every era from the Star League through the ilClan period. Hinsdale Elec on Dover did the same for the Draconis Combine. Andurien AeroTech operated lines for both at Lopez and Westover in Free Worlds League space. The United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora produced both designs for the Outworlds Alliance and later the Raven Alliance. This shared production base helped ensure both types survived the technological regression of the Succession Wars, remaining available across all major factions even as more complex spacecraft fell out of production.

Additional producers served individual factions. Semier Data Tron on Tharkad supplied the Lyran Commonwealth with ST-46s from the Star League through the Civil War era before shutting down during the Jihad. Shipil Company on Skye and Majesty Metals and Manufacturing on Dunianshire each produced the KR-61 without a corresponding ST-46 line. Federated-Boeing Interstellar at Port Simon Shipyards on Galax produced both for the Federated Suns and later the Federated Commonwealth.

Clan versions of both designs emerged centuries into the Succession Wars period. The ST-46C appeared in 2897, initially misidentified by some Inner Sphere observers as captured IS craft given its unarmed civilian configuration. The KR-61C followed in 2851, adopting Clan-grade composite armor for a modest improvement in protection. Full Clan Occupation Zone production of both Clan variants began by 3080, with Clan Jade Falcon's Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten and the Ghost Bear Tseng Facility on Alshain manufacturing both the ST-46C and KR-61C alongside one another, maintaining the paired production pattern established by their Inner Sphere predecessors.

The Aquarius is a 200-ton military aerodyne built around a layered weapons loadout covering multiple engagement ranges. Its primary long-range punch comes from two Long Range Missile launchers, one nose-mounted and one in the left wing, fed by two tons of shared ammunition. For closer work, the nose also mounts a pair of Large Lasers, providing reliable energy firepower without ammunition dependency. Each wing section carries a Six-tube Short-Range Missile launcher and a medium laser, while the aft arc is covered by two additional medium lasers. This arrangement lets the Aquarius engage threats across all arcs without leaving exposed flanks.

With a safe thrust of 4g and maximum thrust of 6g, the Aquarius is considerably faster than the DropShips it is designed to escort, giving it the speed to intercept most threats before they close to effective range. Its thirty-two heat sinks provide adequate dissipation for the energy loadout, though sustained use of both Large Lasers alongside the missile batteries can stress the thermal system. The craft's primary weakness is its modest fuel supply of six tons, which limits operational radius and requires disciplined mission planning on extended patrols.

Developed by Andurien AeroTech and introduced in 2515, the Aquarius Escort was designed to complement the smaller Lyonesse introduced two years earlier. Built to protect DropShips and WarShips operating in contested space, the Aquarius filled the niche between heavyweight aerospace fighters and full combat DropShips, offering the range and firepower to escort capital ships across a system while remaining small enough to dock in standard craft bays. The design quickly became one of Andurien AeroTech's most profitable products, outselling the Lyonesse and earning a reputation as a reliable, versatile escort platform throughout the Star League era. Production eventually ceased following the merger of Andurien AeroTech into Free Worlds Defense Industries and the subsequent decline in demand for dedicated escort craft. The design was resurrected during the Jihad by both the Free Worlds League and the Word of Blake, who produced updated variants for the renewed era of space warfare.

The M1 was produced at the Gibson Federated BattleMechs facility during the Jihad for the Free Worlds League military, representing the League's effort to bring the Aquarius platform up to modern standards. All laser armament was replaced with extended-range equivalents, meaningfully extending effective engagement range. The trade-off was elevated heat generation, requiring disciplined firing cadence during sustained engagements. The M1 served in escort and picket roles throughout the Jihad, protecting League DropShip assets from Word of Blake Pocket WarShip raids. Production ended with the dissolution of the Free Worlds League, and surviving examples were absorbed into the successor states that divided League territory.

Andurien AeroTech released the Aquarius in 2515 to meet demand the Lyonesse had created but could not fully satisfy. Where the Lyonesse was designed for close-in defensive fighting, the Aquarius extended the escort concept outward, using superior speed and a heavier long-range missile loadout to intercept threats before they closed with the vessels it protected. The two designs were complementary by intention, and together they defined the surface-to-orbit escort doctrine of the Star League era. The Aquarius quickly outsold the Lyonesse, becoming Andurien AeroTech's most profitable product and the backbone of Free Worlds League escort operations through the mid-Star League period.

The decline came swiftly after the 2562 merger that created Free Worlds Defense Industries. With heavier aerospace fighters and newer DropShip designs absorbing the escort role, demand for dedicated small craft like the Aquarius collapsed. Production wound down, lines were dismantled or shifted, and both the Aquarius and the Lyonesse passed from active service. The escort small craft role they had built together effectively ceased to exist as a distinct military category in the major powers. In the Periphery, however, Vandenberg Mechanized Industries had watched this decline and drew a different conclusion. When they designed the Tigress in 2790, they explicitly described it as filling the role that the Aquarius and Lyonesse had once held, adapting the concept for the defensive realities of the Taurian Concordat.

The Aquarius returned during the Jihad, when renewed space warfare made the escort role suddenly relevant again. The Free Worlds League produced the M1 variant at Gibson, replacing the standard laser batteries with extended-range models. The Word of Blake's W1 took a different direction, trading most of the weapons suite for an Arrow IV artillery battery, converting the escort craft into a ground-support platform. Both lines served through the Jihad's closing years and both closed when it ended. The escort concept the Aquarius had helped define would not be permanently revived until the Condottiere appeared in 3093, with Nimakachi explicitly citing the Aquarius and Lyonesse as its direct historical predecessors.

The Lyonesse is a 175-ton military aerodyne built for close-range engagements in near-orbit and atmospheric border regions. Its primary long-range weapon is a nose-mounted LRM-20, supplemented by a nose SRM-6 for close work, with both launchers fed by two tons of ammunition each. The craft's wings carry four medium lasers, two per side, providing sustained energy firepower at typical escort engagement ranges. The aft arc is defended by three medium lasers and a small laser, giving the Lyonesse unusually strong rear-quarter coverage against trailing threats.

The Lyonesse's defining strength is the density of its close-in firepower relative to its mass. Against threats that have closed to medium or short range, the full energy battery can be brought to bear with concentrated effect. However, the design has a notable weakness in endurance: five tons of fuel is modest even by small craft standards, making the Lyonesse heavily dependent on nearby tender support for extended operations. With safe thrust of 3g and maximum thrust of 5g, the Lyonesse is less agile than the Aquarius but still considerably faster than most of the DropShips it escorts. Its thirty-five heat sinks manage the sustained energy loadout comfortably in most engagements.

The Lyonesse Escort was Andurien AeroTech's first foray into the escort small craft market, introduced in 2513 as a near-planet protection platform for DropShips and WarShips operating in a system's inner orbits. Designed for short-range, high-intensity combat, the Lyonesse carried armor protection comparable to many light DropShips of its era and packed a formidable close-in weapons array. Its immediate success prompted Andurien AeroTech to develop the larger Aquarius two years later. While the Lyonesse was eventually eclipsed in sales by its sister ship, it maintained a strong reputation for close-in defensive work throughout the Star League era. Like the Aquarius, the Lyonesse was phased out after the formation of Free Worlds Defense Industries, and both designs were briefly revived during the Jihad with updated variants from the Free Worlds League and the Word of Blake.

Produced for the Free Worlds League at Gibson during the Jihad, the M1 upgraded the Lyonesse's laser suite to extended-range equivalents and added PPCs in the wing sections, giving the traditionally close-range platform significantly greater offensive reach. This shift made the M1 better suited to the nature of Jihad-era space combat, where engagements routinely opened at ranges that would have left the original Lyonesse at a disadvantage. Like all Jihad-era revival variants, M1 production ended with the collapse of the League's central government, leaving surviving examples distributed across the successor factions.

When Andurien AeroTech introduced the Lyonesse in 2513, there was no established template for what a dedicated surface-to-orbit escort should be. The Inner Sphere had aerospace fighters for combat and DropShips for transport, but nothing purpose-built to bridge the gap, to ride alongside a DropShip from jump point to atmosphere and back, absorbing fire and returning it. The Lyonesse created that role. Its combination of heavy close-in firepower and armor protection comparable to light DropShips of the era gave convoy commanders a genuine defensive option in near-orbit space for the first time.

The concept proved viable almost immediately. Sales were strong enough that Andurien AeroTech expanded on it just two years later with the larger Aquarius. The Lyonesse and its sister ship became the defining escort small craft of the Star League era, each filling a distinct niche, the Lyonesse as the close-in guardian and the Aquarius as the longer-range interceptor. Together they established what a fleet escort small craft was supposed to be, a standard that would not be seriously challenged or revisited for centuries.

That standard began to erode after Gibson Federated BattleMechs merged with Andurien AeroTech in 2562 to form Free Worlds Defense Industries. Heavier aerospace fighters and some newer DropShip designs had assumed many of the escort roles the Lyonesse and Aquarius had pioneered, and the dedicated escort market was contracting. Both lines were phased out, and by the late twenty-sixth century the escort small craft role the Lyonesse had invented was effectively extinct in most major powers. Surviving examples scattered to Periphery hands and mercenary inventories as their operational lives stretched beyond reasonable support.

The Jihad briefly reversed that trajectory. The Free Worlds League produced the M1 at Gibson, upgrading the laser suite to extended-range models and adding wing-mounted PPCs. The Word of Blake's W1 took a more radical approach, replacing much of the weapons load with an Arrow IV artillery battery. Both lines closed when the Jihad ended. The role the Lyonesse had invented would not find a permanent successor until Nimakachi introduced the Condottiere eighty years later.
