The Mark IX departs from its landing craft relatives most fundamentally in propulsion. Two engine nacelles replace the single nacelle of the Mark VII, providing a safe thrust of 7 and maximum thrust of 11, giving the craft genuine interceptor performance against aerospace fighters. Weighing 200 tons, the Mark IX carries more than double the mass of the Mark VII, with the additional tonnage distributed across a heavier weapons suite, expanded fuel capacity, and substantially more armor.

Armament centers on a forward nose battery of a Large Pulse Laser and an ER Large Laser, suited to extended engagement ranges in deep space. Four medium pulse lasers in the wings provide close-range firepower once the craft closes. Fifteen freezer-model heat sinks manage the energy load. A Beagle active probe allows the Mark IX to support friendly fighters by disrupting hostile ECM fields, a capability that proved decisive in the heavily contested electronic warfare environments of the Jihad. Twenty-seven tons of standard armor protect the hull, concentrated at the nose. The craft carries only three tons of cargo, reflecting its exclusively combat-oriented mission. The dual-nacelle propulsion system is the Mark IX's most visually distinctive feature, making it immediately recognizable alongside the single-nacelle landing craft variants.

The Ares Attack Craft Mark IX is a deep space escort vessel that emerged from the Jihad, representing a radical departure from the landing craft heritage of its name. Produced by Federated Boeing, the Mark IX was developed as large-scale naval operations expanded during the Jihad and the renewed growth of Inner Sphere WarShip fleets created demand for capable close-escort small craft. The design shares the hull dimensions of the Mark VII family but replaces the single engine nacelle with a dual-nacelle propulsion system that nearly doubles available thrust, and trades the landing craft's cargo utility for a heavily armored, deeply armed combat platform. Introduced in 3077 and proven during the campaign for Terra, the Mark IX subsequently attracted license production from Lyran, Republic, and Draconis Combine manufacturers, extending the Ares lineage into the modern era of Inner Sphere naval warfare.

The Mark IX is deployed exclusively in naval escort and deep space defense roles, assigned to WarShip flotillas and large DropShip formations rather than ground assault wings. Federated Suns naval forces were the first to integrate it, fitting Mark IXs into Arondight-class WarShip complements during the Jihad. Its dual nacelles and high thrust give it genuine interceptor capability, and the Beagle active probe makes it particularly effective in ECM-heavy environments. Licensed production spread the design to Lyran, Republic, and Combine fleets in the post-Jihad era, and all four major naval powers continue to operate it into the ilClan period. The Mark IX is rarely encountered in planetary assault roles, its three-ton cargo bay making it unsuitable for the transport missions that define the rest of the Ares family.

The Mark IX traces its origins to the Mk.III Assault Craft of 2451, the dedicated fighter-engagement branch of the original Ares family. IncStar Dynamics built the three-branch family on a single common hull: the Mk.I as the long-range landing craft, the Mk.II as the close attack landing craft, and the Mk.III as the assault craft. All three operated together in HAF wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period before the family was gradually replaced by lighter successor frames from 2476 onward.

The Star League's collapse ended the Ares lineage in its original form. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War after dropping the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward. The long-range landing craft branch survived in the form of the Mark VII, which entered production by 2824 and spread across the Inner Sphere under multiple manufacturers. The close attack landing craft branch had no direct successor. The assault craft branch went entirely dormant, with no active production line carrying the Mk.III's fighter-engagement mission forward.

Universal Air maintained the Ares design archives through the Succession Wars and the Clan Invasion era. After Universal Air merged with Federated Boeing, the combined company possessed both the manufacturing capacity and the institutional knowledge to revisit the dormant assault craft branch. The catalyst arrived with the Jihad and the resurgence of large-scale WarShip operations demanding capable close-escort small craft. Universal Air restarted Ares attack craft production in 3066, and Federated Boeing introduced the substantially upgraded Mark IX in 3077. The Mark IX's combat debut during the campaign for Terra proved the revival, with Federated Suns Arondight crews deploying the design against Word of Blake CASPAR II drone control ships. Its Beagle active probe disrupted hostile ECM coverage and cleared targeting solutions for follow-on Coalition strikes. License production followed to Lyran, Republic, and Draconis Combine manufacturers, reuniting all three surviving lines of the Ares family under active production for the first time since the Star League era.

The Oo-Suzumebachi takes a straightforward approach to its mission, prioritizing protection and firepower over technological sophistication. Its most notable feature is its heavy Ferro-Aluminum armor, with the majority of that protection concentrated on the nose and sides to shield troops during assault approaches. Six anti-missile systems across its wing sections provide layered defense against missile fire, allowing the craft to push through defended airspace that would stop more lightly armored transports.

A powerful main weapon is fitted to clear the landing zone ahead of disembarking troops, and the design handles both atmospheric and space flight, giving commanders flexibility in how and where it is deployed. Its brute-force philosophy means the Ooze will never outperform a dedicated aerospace fighter in a straight engagement, and it carries no pretense of being a high-technology platform. Crew accommodations are basic, with steerage-class sleeping quarters reflecting the craft's utilitarian focus.

The Oo-Suzumebachi, whose name translates to "giant hornet" from Japanese, is a purpose-built assault craft developed by the Draconis Combine following the Second Combine-Dominion War. Designed to deliver battle armor directly into hot landing zones, the first prototype cleared trials at Dover in 3117. Production models quickly became the preferred transport of small-unit battlesuit commanders across the DCMS, earning the nickname "Ooze" from the crews who fly them.

The Oo-Suzumebachi serves the Draconis Combine's special operations and assault infantry forces as a dedicated battle armor transport. It is typically assigned to small-unit battlesuit commanders requiring a rugged, well-armed craft capable of delivering troops under fire. The design pairs effectively with conventional aerospace escort and operates from both DropShip bays and forward ground bases.

The Oo-Suzumebachi was developed in the years following the Second Combine-Dominion War, as the DCMS reconsidered how best to deliver battle armor in contested environments. The first prototype flew at Dover in 3117, and the design entered production the following year.

The craft saw early operational use during the Draconis Reach campaigns of 3139, where several Oozes supported Ryuken-go operations against Davion installations. At Wapakoneta, four craft fought through fixed defenses to prevent a Davion counterattack from striking a Dragoon column. Using their anti-missile systems to suppress defending LRM batteries, the Oozes delivered troops directly onto fortified positions and held the bridgehead long enough to secure the Dragoon withdrawal.

By 3144, the design had become a recognized tool of the DCMS's assault infantry doctrine. During the conquest of Cimeron against the Fifth Robinson Strikers, elements of the Twenty-second New Samarkand Regulars used a small force of Oozes to insert battlesuit infantry onto an enemy air base while the regiment's fighters and DropShips staged a diversion. The operation eliminated the LCT's aerospace assets and forced the Fifth to withdraw off-world.

The Zhen Niao carries only a pair of Extended-Range Medium Lasers, both mounted in the aft arc, and a single Space Mine Dispenser. The lasers provide minimal self-defense capability against pursuing aerospace fighters, while the mine dispenser doubles as an intrasystem weapon and as a prop supporting the craft's cover as a civilian customs vessel. The design makes no pretense of being a front-line combat asset. Its ferro-aluminum armor, at twelve tons, is adequate for a craft whose primary survivability depends on not being identified rather than on absorbing punishment.

The electronics suite defines what the Zhen Niao actually is. A Hyperspectral Imager provides exceptional surface-scan capability from orbit. A Beagle Active Probe extends detection range well beyond the craft's visual profile. A Guardian ECM Suite degrades enemy targeting and sensor systems, supporting both the craft's own protection and its civilian impersonation role. The Improved Communications design quirk extends the Zhen Niao's data relay range, allowing intelligence gathered in orbit to be transmitted to ground or DropShip commanders in near real time.

The craft's limitations are clear. Safe thrust of 2.5g and a maximum of 4g leave it vulnerable to dedicated interception if its cover is blown. Its crew of four, all accommodated in Steerage-class quarters, reflects the austere operational profile. The Zhen Niao is built to gather and transmit intelligence, not to fight its way out of trouble. Commands that deploy it expecting anything beyond its reconnaissance role will find it wanting.

The Zhen Niao, whose name translates roughly as "Poisonfeather Bird," is a Small Craft designed and produced by Rashpur-Owens Incorporated on Capella for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces. Introduced in 3101, it was conceived not as a conventional combat vessel but as an armed noncombatant, a platform for electronic warfare and orbital reconnaissance capable of operating without fighter escort. The CCAF adopted it rapidly, recognizing its value as an intelligence asset that could fly random powered orbits, blend into civilian intrasystem traffic, and deny enemy aerospace forces the predictable patterns they relied on to hunt satellite-class craft. Understated in appearance and deceptive in purpose, the Zhen Niao represents the Confederation's preference for asymmetric capabilities over brute-force aerospace superiority.

The Zhen Niao serves in CCAF aerospace screening and electronic warfare assignments, deployed in pairs from dedicated Capellan DropShips to maintain mutual support during extended independent operations. Its orbital profile mimics civilian intrasystem traffic, and crews are trained to maintain patterns consistent with commercial vessels. The craft's fuel capacity supports lengthy missions without tender contact, making it well suited for advance reconnaissance assignments ahead of conventional operations.

Commands tasked with planetary assault or large-scale interdiction benefit most from the Zhen Niao. Its limited armament makes direct engagement inadvisable, and commanders who treat it as a combat asset rather than a reconnaissance platform misuse it. Used correctly, it provides actionable intelligence at a cost and risk profile well below that of a dedicated aerospace fighter screen.

Rashpur-Owens Incorporated developed the Zhen Niao in the years following the Jihad, responding to CCAF requirements for a dedicated electronic warfare and orbital reconnaissance platform that could operate without an escort footprint. The design entered service in 3101, marking an expansion of Rashpur-Owens' traditional focus on large aerospace vessels into the Small Craft category. The Capellan Confederation integrated the type into DropShip operations quickly, typically deploying pairs of craft on intelligence-gathering missions ahead of conventional forces.

The Warrior House Offensive of 3112 provided the Zhen Niao's first significant operational test. Two craft deployed from a Capellan DropShip to make competing orbital passes over Republic-held worlds, gathering first-scan intelligence on planetary defenses and troop dispositions before the assault began. Davion aerospace fighters rose to intercept them. The two Zhen Niaos used their electronic systems and fuel reserves to run, laying minefields and counting on their ECM to protect them. Only one escaped. The surviving craft's data, however, proved critical to the offensive's initial success, and the engagement was studied afterward as a demonstration of both the type's value and its vulnerability when denied the element of surprise.

Later operations at Tikonov revealed a different dimension of the craft's capability. Operating covertly from Capellan merchant DropShips over an extended period, Zhen Niao crews gathered detailed intelligence on a succession of Republic worlds prior to formal military operations. RAF analysts determined after the fact that the craft had maintained orbit for nearly a week at a stretch, refueling at Capellan merchants in transit, before Confederation ground forces moved. The intelligence contributed materially to the depth of the Capellan advance through Republic lines.

By the Dark Age, the Zhen Niao had earned a quiet reputation within the CCAF as one of the more effective surveillance platforms in the Confederation's aerospace inventory, prized by commanders who understood how to use it and largely invisible to those who did not.

The Caerleon's defining characteristic is its protection. More than twenty tons of ferro-aluminum armor give the craft a fortress-like durability that shields its troop complement through intense defensive fire. Its armament centers on a nose battery of two Light Gauss Rifles and two LRM-15 launchers, the latter fitted with Artemis IV fire control systems to improve salvo accuracy at range. Two ER Medium Lasers cover the aft arc, providing a deterrent against pursuit and a close-in option during boarding approaches. The craft carries two tons of Light Gauss Rifle ammunition and four tons for the LRM racks, supporting extended operations without resupply.

The Caerleon benefits from Easy to Maintain and Fast Reload design quirks, keeping it operational under austere field conditions and allowing its weapons to be cycled quickly during close-quarters assaults. These practical advantages helped offset persistent criticism that the engine is underpowered for an assault craft, limiting acceleration and reducing the ability to chase or evade faster opponents. Nimakachi's engineers consistently declined to address either the engine or the firepower concerns, citing favorable feedback from the troopers the craft served.

The design's most serious liability is a well-documented atmospheric flight instability that makes precision planetside approaches hazardous and has caused a number of combat losses. This flaw is inherent to the airframe and has not been corrected in any production run.

Named for an ancient fortress associated with the legendary King Arthur, the Caerleon entered service in 3093 as Nimakachi Fusion Products Limited's dedicated battle armor transport, designed to carry a full platoon into assault operations. Built at the Dalton orbital yards, the craft spread quickly from its Free Worlds League origins into the broader mercenary market, where its combination of heavy armor and reliable troop-carrying capacity earned it a loyal following. Two roles define its service career: boarding operations against enemy DropShips and JumpShips, and direct battlefield support for the infantry it delivers. Nimakachi's engineers emphasized durability and ease of maintenance over outright speed or firepower, a philosophy that critics questioned but the troopers who relied on it consistently validated.

The Caerleon excels in boarding operations and assault landings, where its heavy armor absorbs defensive fire long enough to deliver its battle armor platoon. Boarding missions represent the design's optimal employment profile, with the atmospheric flight instability being largely irrelevant in vacuum operations. Operators learned to prefer orbital insertion profiles when circumstances permitted, reserving contested atmospheric approaches for situations where no alternative existed.

Notable individual Caerleons include the Phantom, a craft of unknown affiliation and ownership that operates opportunistically throughout League and Periphery space, targeting damaged or disabled DropShips for capture. Its mismatched battle armor squads secure targets before escorting them to an Invader-class JumpShip. The Phantom was last reported active in 3144 before disappearing from observation. The Chatelain serves with the Second Andurien Guard's Escort Group Three under Commander Daniel Gallery, frequently leading the advance into enemy territory on raids. Under the direction of Master Banner Jillian Leigh Foley, the Chatelain's boarding party has captured six enemy vessels since 3138.

Nimakachi Fusion Products Limited introduced the Caerleon in 3093 at their Dalton orbital production facility, developing it as a dedicated battle armor transport during the political realignment that followed the dissolution of the Free Worlds League. Backed by Oriente Protectorate procurement contracts, the design found ready buyers across the successor states and the mercenary market, where its reputation for durability and low maintenance burden made it an attractive option for commands needing a reliable assault craft on limited budgets.

The Caerleon's combat record grew quickly. During the Victoria War, the Sixth Oriente Hussars employed Caerleons at Bentley in a boarding action against a Capellan Seeker-class DropShip breaking orbit. Two craft intercepted the vessel at the edge of its drive envelope, concentrating fire on the engines before marines breached the hull from two points simultaneously. Once the DropShip was secured, the Hussars discovered the planetary governor and his family aboard. The operation validated the Caerleon's primary design role and helped establish its reputation as an effective boarding platform across the former League states.

The atmospheric limitations cost the design dearly on Pella II in February 3104. When the Eighth Orloff Aerospace committed their Caerleons to continuous troop lifts under heavy antiaircraft fire during fighting between combined Red Lancers and Roman's Mounted Fusiliers forces and the Eighth Orloff Grenadiers, seven craft were lost. Three of the surviving Caerleons diverted directly into the path of advancing Capellan BattleMechs to cover the DDOCFH withdrawal, demonstrating the willingness of Caerleon crews to accept extreme risk for their passengers. The Pella II engagement became a cautionary example of misapplying the Caerleon in sustained contested atmospheric operations.

Production continued under the Oriente Protectorate through the Dark Age period. When the Oriente Protectorate collapsed and the Free Worlds League reconstituted, the Dalton facility returned to FWL stewardship, and the Caerleon remained in production as one of several Nimakachi designs serving the new League's military and export markets.

The Condottiere carries 19.5 tons of Ferro-Aluminum armor, with a notable concentration forward, giving it strong protection against direct-fire threats when interposing itself between an attacker and its charges. The weapons suite covers multiple engagement ranges, combining nose-mounted long-range firepower with wing-mounted systems for medium and close-range threats. Maximum thrust matches that of the Lyonesse, providing adequate speed for most escort intercept scenarios without exceptional pursuit performance.

The Condottiere's defining characteristic is its ease of handling. The control systems were designed with automation in mind, significantly reducing crew instruction time and making the craft well suited as a training vessel alongside its combat role. A nine-ton fuel tank gives it longer operational legs than the Star League-era escort designs it replaced. A single-ton cargo bay with one access door allows the craft to carry a small battle armor contingent for extravehicular operations, adding a boarding and inspection capability absent from purely combat-focused escort craft. The Condottiere's focus on affordability means it is competitive rather than outstanding in any single performance metric, and operators who require extreme performance in one area may find it lacking.

Produced by Nimakachi Fusion Products Ltd. and introduced in 3093, the Condottiere Assault Craft was designed to fill the escort capability gap created by the Jihad's devastation of major fleet assets across the Inner Sphere. The destruction of WarShips and the proliferation of Pocket WarShip technology had returned spacefaring vessels to the list of viable military targets for the first time in generations. Civilian operators, mercenary commands, and smaller military formations found themselves without effective protection for their DropShips and JumpShips. Nimakachi produced the Condottiere as a cost-effective answer, balancing firepower, ease of handling, and low maintenance costs to create a platform accessible to buyers well outside the major house militaries. The craft's combination of practical design and aggressive marketing through lease arrangements made it one of the most widely distributed escort small craft of the early Dark Age.

The Condottiere is found throughout the Inner Sphere, serving with large mercenary commands, minor planetary garrisons, and individual DropShip operators seeking practical escort protection. Its lease availability through Nimakachi Fusion Products Ltd. means the craft appears in service with factions that would not normally have the procurement budget for a purpose-built military small craft. The combination of easy handling characteristics and available crew instruction programs also makes it common in training roles alongside combat assignments. Nimakachi produces the Condottiere on Dalton, and the design has continued to see production through the ilClan era.

The role that the Lyonesse had invented in 2513, perfected by the Aquarius two years later, and kept alive by the Tigress in the Periphery for three centuries, had been effectively absent from the Inner Sphere for generations when Nimakachi Fusion Products Ltd. revived it in 3093. The Jihad had returned capital ships and WarShips to the list of viable combat targets, and the destruction of major fleet assets had left civilian operators, mercenary commands, and smaller military formations without effective protection for their DropShips and JumpShips. Nimakachi saw the gap clearly and designed the Condottiere to fill it, naming the Aquarius and Lyonesse explicitly as the ancestral designs it was meant to succeed.

Where the original escorts had been purpose-built for major house navies, Nimakachi aimed the Condottiere at the wider market those navies could not reach. Lease arrangements alongside direct sales made the craft accessible to operators who could not afford outright purchase. Easy handling characteristics reduced crew instruction time and made it viable as a training vessel, broadening its appeal further. The Condottiere spread quickly across the Inner Sphere, appearing in large mercenary commands and with individual DropShip operators alike. One unusual feature of many early lease contracts, a mutual nonaggression clause between Nimakachi-leased craft, created the notable embarrassment at Benedict in 3139 when opposing forces both fielded leased Condottieres that ignored each other to attack the opposing DropShips instead. Nimakachi subsequently revised its standard terms.

Production continued through the Oriente Protectorate era and into the ilClan period, with Nimakachi maintaining the line on Dalton. The Condottiere had accomplished what the Jihad-era Aquarius and Lyonesse revivals had not, a permanent restoration of the escort small craft as a distinct and viable military category across the Inner Sphere. The lineage that the Lyonesse began in 2513 had found its most durable inheritor.

A full quarter of the NL-45's mass is devoted to combat systems, an unusually high proportion for a small craft of its size. The centerpiece of the design is an enhanced electronic warfare suite that makes the Gunboat roughly twenty percent harder to target than an unaugmented aerospace fighter of comparable size. This ECM capability proves particularly valuable during close-range engagements where the craft's modest weapons might otherwise leave it vulnerable to heavier opponents.

The NL-45 carries a battle armor bay sufficient to transport a single Point of battle armor, with the bay designed to support orbital combat drops. This capability is the craft's primary attraction for crews assigned to boarding and interdiction duties. Outside the battle armor bay, internal space is cramped, with average weapons range and a small cargo hold that together limit the Gunboat's ability to sustain extended independent patrols. These constraints keep the NL-45 tethered to its parent WarShip or station, functioning best as a short-range picket rather than a long-endurance patrol platform.

The NL-45 Gunboat is a combat picket small craft built by the United Outworlders Corporation at their Ramora factory for the Raven Alliance. Introduced in 3094, the NL-45 continues the tradition of NL-series military transports begun during the Star League era. Designed to fill a role that the corporation's civilian craft could not, the Gunboat serves as a patrol and light escort vessel for Clan naval assets. Since its debut the NL-45 has proven a valuable export product, becoming the default platform for any Clan needing a small craft to patrol near space, deploy boarding parties to armed vessels, or screen larger formations during orbital operations.

The base NL-45 is the sole production configuration of the Gunboat. Its combination of enhanced electronic warfare systems, battle armor transport capability, and orbital drop support makes it well suited to the Raven Alliance's doctrine of leveraging naval superiority through distributed small craft screens and rapid boarding actions against both military and pirate targets.

The NL-45 was developed by the United Outworlders Corporation to meet a specific gap in the Raven Alliance's naval order of battle. While the Alliance possessed significant WarShip and DropShip assets inherited from Clan Snow Raven's long tradition of naval excellence, it lacked a purpose-built small craft for the picket and boarding roles that its growing territorial responsibilities demanded. UOC, a Periphery manufacturer with limited military production experience, adapted existing civilian small craft expertise to produce the Gunboat, filling a niche that more established Clan manufacturers had neglected.

The NL-45 saw its first major combat deployment during the Raven Alliance's invasion of Kirbyville. Beta Galaxy used the Gunboats extensively to secure the system, dispatching them to nearly every manned satellite in orbit. Resistance was met with autocannon fire directed at life support systems, quickly discouraging further opposition. When the Third Periphery Guard committed to atmospheric entry, the Gunboats shifted to an aerospace screening role, exploiting their ECM suites to offset the numerical advantage held by defending fighters. A second wave of NL-45s then accompanied Arcadia-class DropShips to deliver battle armor directly into the capital while the Arcadias engaged ground targets.

The Gunboat has also featured prominently in Lyran operations against the Jade Falcon Golden Ordun. Falcon WarShips routinely deployed NL-45s as defensive screens, leveraging the craft's ECM capabilities to complicate attacks by Lyran aerospace units. During the Lyran assault on Wroclaw, NL-45s formed part of the defensive barrier that forced attackers into close range where the Falcon fleet's heavier armament dominated. The craft's most notable defensive action occurred at Timkovichi, where a pair of NL-45s generated an electronics screen that spoofed three of five nuclear weapons launched at the WarShip White Aerie. A third Gunboat lurking close to the vessel destroyed the remaining two warheads, an action that remains the closest the Lyrans have come to destroying a Falcon WarShip since the Golden Ordun invasion began.

The heart of the Würger is the Lockheed/CBM Progeny II tactical computer. This system unifies the craft's offensive and defensive electronics under a single management framework, and also integrates the cooling system and engine control. The Progeny II takes hundreds of sensor readings per second from myriad onboard sensors, making continuous synergistic adjustments to maximize the effectiveness of each installed system. This allows the Würger to respond rapidly to changing battlefield conditions without relying on pilot interpretation alone.

As a small craft optimized for orbital interdiction and point-defense screening, the Würger trades the raw firepower of heavier aerospace platforms for precision sensor integration and responsiveness. It performs best in engagements against other small craft and missiles rather than capital-scale targets, and operates effectively in the confined tactical space around a Pocket WarShip or space station. This specialization carries tradeoffs: without numerical support, the Würger cannot sustain prolonged engagements against dedicated assault craft, and its point-defense role leaves it reliant on coordinated wing tactics to compensate for individual firepower limits.

The Würger Assault Craft is a purpose-built small craft developed by Lockheed/CBM on Furillo for the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, entering service in 3099. It was designed to fill the growing need for dedicated orbital screening platforms in an era when Pocket WarShips had become a fixture of Inner Sphere naval operations. Rather than relying on aerospace fighters to screen capital ships and space stations, the LCAF sought a specialized craft optimized for missile interdiction and close-in defense work. The Würger represents Lockheed/CBM's answer to that requirement, building on earlier small craft concepts to deliver a more capable and electronically integrated platform suited to the demands of Dark Age naval warfare.

The Würger serves as an orbital escort and interdiction platform within the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, most commonly deployed in wings assigned to Pocket WarShip screens and system defense stations. It performs best in coordinated groups, where numerical advantage over larger assault craft compensates for its individual firepower limits. The type has seen consistent use along the Lyran-Clan border, where the threat of orbital bombardment and deep-space boarding actions has made mobile, responsive small craft a standing priority for LCAF commanders.

The Jihad fundamentally reshaped naval warfare across the Inner Sphere. The prolific use of anti-ship missiles against DropShips and capital ships prompted widespread adoption of robust point-defense systems, seen in vessels like the Interdictor and the Arondight-class DropShips. By 3094, the NL-45 had become the first small craft purpose-built for missile defense and interdiction, establishing a new category of dedicated naval support craft. The Würger followed in 3099 as the next step in that evolution, incorporating the more integrated sensor and control architecture of the Progeny II computer and pushing the concept further toward a true fleet screening platform.

The design's capabilities were demonstrated during the Jade Falcon offensive of 3143. Archon Vedet Brewer had positioned substantial forces to defend Westerstede, including multiple Würger wings operating alongside two Bastion-class and one Battlesat-class system defense stations. When Jade Falcon DropShips arrived, they split into three groups: one to engage the LCAF fighter screen, one to push 'Mech transports toward the planet, and a third of battle taxis held in reserve to board the stations once the screen was cleared.

For four hours the LCAF fighter screen and the Jade Falcons fought to a standstill. Engine damage then forced the LCS Akfata, an Isegrim-class assault DropShip, to withdraw, and the Clan forces saw their opening, burning hard for the defense stations. The waiting Würger wings launched from their bays and engaged the Clan craft during the vulnerable deceleration burn. Outnumbered more than two-to-one, the Jade Falcon assault craft eventually withdrew to their transports. Five battle taxis breached the screen and delivered boarding parties, but all were repelled with minimal casualties among the defenders.

The Würgers then rejoined the wider dogfight, giving the LCAF fighter wing time to return to the stations and rearm. When those fighters came back less than half an hour later, the Clan forces retreated to their jump point. Though the archon ultimately ordered the abandonment of Westerstede in favor of fortifying Tharkad, the Würgers had maintained the LCAF's orbital presence throughout, denying the Jade Falcons air support and reconnaissance for the duration of the planetside campaign.

The Mówáng is a 100-ton Civilian Aerodyne Small Craft powered by a standard fusion powerplant delivering a safe thrust of 4G and a maximum thrust of 6G, providing adequate performance for intra-system transit between planetary surfaces, orbital stations, and jump points. Fuel capacity supports routine system hops without requiring intermediate resupply. The craft's three-man crew is drawn from the employing noble's personal staff, valued for discretion rather than combat experience.

Passenger accommodations are modest but well-appointed for a vessel of this class. A single first-class stateroom serves the primary passenger, while two steerage-rated cabins accommodate aides or companions. Cargo capacity is limited to five and a half tons, accessed through a single cargo door, which is sufficient for personal effects, gifts, or contraband at the owner's discretion.

Armor protection amounts to just two and a half tons of standard plating, arranged to deflect debris rather than withstand weapons fire. The Mówáng carries no armament whatsoever. These limitations reflect deliberate design choices: military protection would raise costs and attract inspection. The craft's entire defensive strategy rests on appearing unremarkable. Its construction is intentionally within the manufacturing capability of any modestly industrialized world, which is reflected in its price tag of roughly 3.5 million C-bills.

The Mówáng-class Courier is a compact civilian Small Craft conceived during the early First Succession War to serve the personal transport needs of Capellan Confederation nobility. Commissioned by the House of Scions in 2835, the design was built around simplicity, passenger comfort, and low production cost. The House declared an open manufacturing license immediately upon introduction, inviting any world with adequate industrial capacity to build the craft without restriction. That decision spread the Mówáng across dozens of systems within a few generations, making it among the most widely distributed personal spacecraft in the Inner Sphere. Lightly built and unarmed, the vessel relies on its mundane appearance and near-universal familiarity to pass scrutiny wherever it operates.

The Clandestine variant operates exclusively as a covert assault transport for Word of Blake operatives during the Jihad period. Outwardly indistinguishable from a standard Mówáng, the craft approaches its objective concealed within the traffic of a civilian DropShip or JumpShip, then separates for its attack run. The Angel ECM suite is activated before approach to jam communications and degrade tracking, followed by bombing of the target site. Two Level Is of battle armor are then deployed for ground operations, and the craft stands by to extract the troops or continue suppressing first responders with additional bomb runs. The Internal Bomb Bay is the primary stand-off weapon, used both before and after troop deployment.

The Mówáng-class Courier emerged in the early years of the First Succession War, when established DropShip service networks grew unreliable and Capellan nobles sought alternatives for private intra-system travel. The House of Scions, the aristocratic body overseeing Capellan nobility, sponsored the design with specific requirements: the craft had to be affordable, simple to build, and comfortable enough for a Diem to use as a personal vehicle. The open manufacturing license declared in 2835 was a deliberate policy choice, intended to maximize production across the Confederation's many worlds rather than concentrate output at a handful of licensed facilities. Within decades, the design had spread throughout the Capellan Confederation and was being produced by local manufacturers on dozens of worlds.

Throughout the Succession Wars the Mówáng occupied a quiet but persistent niche. Capellan Diems used them to travel between worlds in their multi-planetary holdings, convey valuables, and move goods, licit or otherwise, beyond the reach of formal customs networks. Their unremarkable profile meant that military and customs patrols rarely subjected them to serious scrutiny. As the design spread beyond the Confederation, nobles and wealthy merchants in neighboring states acquired them for the same reasons. By the time of the Clan Invasion, the Mówáng had become common enough in Inner Sphere system traffic that a single craft could move through most ports without comment.

That anonymity proved dangerous during the Jihad. In 3073, the Word of Blake acquired a number of Mówáng hulls provided by Kali Liao and modified them as covert assault transports. The conversions stripped out passenger quarters, installed battle armor bays capable of carrying two Level Is of troops, reduced the engine output to free internal volume, increased armor protection to four tons, and fitted an Angel ECM suite. The modified craft were used as clandestine insertion vehicles, exploiting the Mówáng's civilian identity to approach targets aboard passenger DropShips or JumpShips before executing attack runs. Most of these converted hulls were destroyed or captured before the Jihad concluded, but the episode left a residual wariness. Several jurisdictions instituted enhanced inspection requirements for Mówáng-type craft in the early Republic era, and the vessel's reputation as an innocent courier was never fully restored.

The 'Scarab' retains the S-7A's external profile and basic propulsion, making visual identification virtually impossible without a thorough inspection. The forward cargo bay has been gutted and repurposed to house a 10-ton booby trap connected to the engineering module. Ten heat sinks support the trap mechanism, replacing the original module's standard configuration. A second bay retains 19 tons of cargo capacity, while a third accommodates a six-ton jump infantry platoon for the boarding party.

The craft carries no weapons. Its offensive capability rests entirely on the threat of detonation: once docked to a target vessel, the pirate crew can credibly threaten to destroy both ships unless the crew surrenders. The jump infantry deploy only after compliance or when the threat must be pressed directly.

The S7-P 'Scarab' is a pirate field conversion of the S-7A Bus chassis, first documented in 3073, designed to appear as an ordinary civilian shuttle while concealing a hidden booby trap. The origin of the design is believed to be Tortuga, though producer and technician records remain unknown. The conversion exploits the ubiquity of the S-7A to gain access to JumpShips and DropShips under false pretenses, turning a common transit craft into a coercive weapon.

The 'Scarab' is deployed by attaching to a target JumpShip at zenith or nadir jump points under a distress or routine transit pretense. Once limpeted, the pirate crew uses the booby trap threat to compel surrender without direct combat. The jump infantry platoon provides a boarding force if the crew complies or if the threat must be pressed by force.

The first confirmed use of the 'Scarab' took place in 3073, when a commercial Invader-class JumpShip responded to a distress call near the zenith jump point of Erod's Escape. A Buccaneer-class DropShip nearby sent what appeared to be a standard S-7A shuttle to assist, while pirates held back the bulk of the crew. Once docked, the pirate leader declared the booby trap on the engine would detonate unless the JumpShip's captain surrendered his vessel and all attached DropShips.

The Invader's captain refused and began evacuating the captured areas. The pirates boarded a Trojan-class DropShip still docked to the JumpShip and decoupled. As the Trojan cleared, the pirate leader triggered the trap, breaking the Invader's spine and killing nearly all aboard. Two further JumpShip captures using similar shuttles were subsequently reported, prompting ComStar to issue warnings across the region.

The Mk.III Assault Craft substantially upgrades both propulsion and protection over the base Ares design. Its more powerful primitive fusion engine nearly doubles the maximum thrust of the Mk.I, allowing the craft to pursue and intercept enemy fighters rather than simply defend. Heavier armor and additional heat sinks reflect the shift to a direct combat role.

The Mark VII carries six medium lasers across the nose, wings, and aft positions, supplemented by two nose-mounted small lasers. A Fusion 200 engine provides safe thrust 4 and maximum thrust 6. Thirteen tons of standard armor protect the hull, with nose concentration. A 31-ton cargo bay is retained alongside the weapons systems. The Mark VII's VTOL hover capability allows it to land in rough terrain without prepared strips, an advantage over conventional aerodyne designs that require prepared surfaces. The design's reliance on short-range energy weapons makes it most effective in close engagements, and it performs poorly against opponents who can maintain standoff range.

The Mark VII-C substitutes Clan medium pulse lasers for IS medium lasers and fits Clan double heat sinks, improving thermal efficiency while retaining the same combat silhouette. Clan standard armor runs one ton lighter than the IS version but provides superior protection values.

The Ares Assault Craft represents the combat-hardened branch of the Ares small craft lineage, tracing its origins to the primitive Mk.III of 2451 and evolving into the Mark VII, one of the most widely produced military landing craft in the Inner Sphere. Developed by IncStar Dynamics as a dedicated fighter-engagement variant, the Mk.III prioritized combat capability while retaining limited cargo capacity. Its heavier engine and upgraded armor set a template that later designers refined during the Succession Wars into the standard-technology Mark VII, produced at multiple factories and fielded by every major Inner Sphere power. The Clan adaptation, designated the Mark VII-C, brought advanced Clan technology to the same proven airframe, completing the long evolution from a primitive Age of War design into a craft that would serve in front-line roles across the entire Inner Sphere and Clan space well into the ilClan era.

The Mk.III Assault Craft was assigned to HAF aerospace wings tasked with direct fighter suppression during landing operations. Unlike the Mk.II, which operated as part of landing craft formations, the Mk.III could operate independently and served with WarShip and JumpShip flotillas as a close-escort asset. Its enhanced thrust allowed crews to pursue and engage enemy fighters rather than simply defend during descent, and HAF squadrons valued it as both a deterrent and an active interceptor. The design entered service in 2451 and remained the most capable combat craft in the Ares family through the late Age of War, keeping its front-line assignment well into the Star League era even after the introduction of the lighter successor frames.

IncStar Dynamics introduced the Mk.III Assault Craft in 2451 as the third branch of the original Ares family, joining the Mk.I long-range landing craft and the Mk.II close attack landing craft on the same base hull. Where the Mk.I carried cargo and the Mk.II provided escort suppression, the Mk.III was built for direct fighter engagement. Its more powerful engine gave it the thrust to pursue and intercept, and reinforced armor allowed it to absorb damage that would have disabled the other marks. All three designs operated together in HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period, each branch complementing the others on contested planetary approaches.

The fall of the Star League and the Succession Wars stripped away the manufacturing base that supported the original Ares family. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War, having already dropped the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward. By 2824, a simplified but robust successor emerged: the Mark VII, the standard-technology heir to the Mk.I long-range landing craft branch. Produced at factories across the Successor States and the Taurian Concordat, the Mark VII carried the landing craft lineage forward while the close attack branch of the Mk.II was absorbed into broader doctrine and the assault craft branch of the Mk.III lay dormant.

The Mark VII-C emerged in 2841 with Clan technology. Clan Ghost Bear produced it at their Tseng Facility in orbit around Alshain, and Clan Jade Falcon added production at the Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten in 3074. Both the IS Mark VII and the Clan Mark VII-C share the introduction year of 2841 despite the decades of isolation between the two civilizations, leading historians to conclude that both designs evolved independently from a shared earlier ancestor rather than one copying the other.

The assault craft branch of the family did not stay dormant permanently. Universal Air maintained the original Ares design archives through the Succession Wars and the Clan Invasion era. After merging with Federated Boeing, the company restarted Ares attack craft production in 3066 and introduced the Mark IX in 3077, completing the revival of the third branch and reuniting all three lines of the original Ares family under active production for the first time since the Star League era.

The Mk.II distinguishes itself from the Mk.I primarily in its offensive armament. Three large lasers supplement the existing weapons layout, dramatically increasing the craft's ability to engage enemy fighters and ground targets at extended range. This heavier weapons load demands more heat management, and the Mk.II carries additional heat sinks over the base design to handle the added thermal output. The reduced cargo capacity is a deliberate trade, reflecting the craft's shift from transport to fire support.

The primitive fusion engine and armor profile closely mirror those of the Mk.I, providing the same basic mobility and protection envelope. Forward and aft defense is retained through the same combination of nose and aft medium lasers that proved effective on the base landing craft, giving the Mk.II adequate self-protection even when operating away from formation cover. The aerodyne configuration is identical to the base design, keeping maintenance and training requirements consistent across the family. Like all Ares variants, the Mk.II carries the performance limitations common to primitive-era aerospace design, including reduced maneuverability compared to later standard-technology successors.

The Ares Close Assault Landing Craft, designated the Mk.II, emerged just six years after the Mk.I as a purpose-built fire support variant of the Ares family. Developed by IncStar Dynamics, the Mk.II replaced a portion of the standard landing craft's cargo capacity with an additional battery of large lasers, transforming the design from a transport with self-defense weaponry into a genuine close-support gunship. Where the Mk.I was optimized for cargo delivery, the Mk.II was intended to serve as a heavy escort, clearing fighter screens and suppressing ground targets as the cargo-laden landing craft completed their runs. The design was fielded by the Hegemony Armed Forces alongside the Mk.I, operating in mixed squadrons that paired the Mk.II's fire support with the Mk.I's cargo capacity and the Mk.III's fighter-engagement role.

The Mk.II Close Assault Landing Craft was assigned in small numbers to HAF landing craft wings, typically one or two craft per squadron. Its role was strictly fire support: clearing fighter screens and providing heavy ground-attack capability as Mk.I craft completed their cargo deliveries. Mk.II crews developed aggressive approach profiles, closing quickly and engaging hostile fighters before breaking off to allow the cargo craft through. The design was not assigned independent transport duties, relying on the Mk.I for cargo work and the Mk.III for direct fighter engagement. Deployment alongside sister craft in mixed squadrons allowed each variant to focus on its designed mission, a combined-arms approach that defined HAF landing operations throughout the Age of War.

The Hegemony Armed Forces recognized early that the Mk.I, however capable as a cargo carrier, could not simultaneously deliver heavy armor and provide the concentrated fire support needed to suppress determined fighter opposition. IncStar Dynamics' solution was to build the Mk.II Close Assault Landing Craft on the same base hull as the Mk.I, introducing it in 2444 alongside the Mk.III Assault Craft. The three designs formed a deliberate family: the Mk.I as the long-range landing craft branch, the Mk.II as the close attack landing craft branch, and the Mk.III as the dedicated fighter-engagement branch. Sharing a common hull simplified logistics, training, and maintenance across the three types.

The Mk.II served in mixed HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period, operating alongside its two sister designs. Crews developed aggressive escort profiles, closing to maximum effective laser range before breaking off to allow Mk.I cargo craft through contested airspace. The type earned a reputation for sustained close-range fire, often remaining in hostile airspace longer than doctrine required to ensure the landing craft completed their drops.

When the redesigned Mk.IV successor frame arrived in 2476, the close assault escort role was gradually absorbed into the Mk.III Assault Craft lineage, which offered superior thrust and maneuverability for the fighter-engagement mission. The Mk.II transitioned to second-line duties and was eventually superseded entirely by the Mark VII following the Star League's collapse. The close attack landing craft branch itself did not produce a direct named successor the way the long-range landing craft branch produced the Mark VII, or the assault craft branch produced the Ares Mark IX. The Mk.II's escort role was instead folded into the broader capabilities of those surviving lines.

The Ares Mk.I carries an armament designed to punch through fighter screens before they can close. Two medium lasers in the nose give the craft forward bite, while a pair of LRM-15 launchers in the wings extend its reach to ranges where opposing fighters struggle to respond effectively. Two additional medium lasers in the aft position protect against pursuit. Sixteen heat sinks manage the thermal load from sustained fire. The primitive fusion engine delivers a safe thrust of 3 and maximum thrust of 5, adequate for atmospheric transit and planetary approaches but not suited to prolonged deep-space pursuit.

The cargo bay holds 65 tons behind two doors, large enough to accommodate the heavy tracked vehicles of the era. Twenty-four tons of primitive armor protect the hull, with heavier concentration at the nose to resist head-on fighter attacks during descent. The aerodyne configuration makes the craft dependent on prepared surfaces or low-speed hover approaches, a constraint later marks addressed more fully. Crew requirements consist of a single officer and four enlisted personnel, modest for a vessel of this firepower.

The Ares Landing Craft was the Terran Hegemony's answer to the hazardous problem of orbit-to-surface transport under fire. Designed by IncStar Dynamics and introduced in 2438, the Ares replaced a generation of converted merchant vessels that either sacrificed cargo capacity for self-defense weapons or lacked the firepower to survive contested planetary approaches. The Hegemony Armed Forces commissioned the design around the time of the Ares Conventions, and the craft's name reflected that era's cooperative military spirit. A 65-ton cargo bay, a heavy weapons array, and primitive but robust armor made the Ares the definitive combat landing craft of its generation, providing HAF ground commanders reliable orbit-to-surface access under conditions that would have destroyed earlier designs. Its success prompted IncStar Dynamics to develop several specialized variants tailored to the diverse combat roles that emerged from early Age of War operations.

The Mk.I served as the primary orbit-to-surface transport of the Hegemony Armed Forces during the Age of War, assigned to deliver heavy armor and cargo to contested planetary surfaces. Typical mission profiles paired the Mk.I with Mk.II Close Assault craft, which suppressed enemy fighter cover while the standard landing craft completed their cargo runs. The 65-ton bay accommodated heavy tracked vehicles up to the largest battle tanks of the era. HAF commanders deployed the design in squadron formations, assigning individual craft to specific armored or mechanized units for the duration of ground campaigns. Its primitive technology and limited performance envelope restricted the Mk.I to conventional atmospheric operations, rarely encountered in deep-space or orbital roles beyond basic transit runs between DropShips and landing zones.

Before the Ares entered service, the Hegemony Armed Forces relied on converted merchant craft that proved dangerously inadequate under contested conditions. These vessels either carried too little self-defense weaponry to deter aggressive fighter screens, or sacrificed cargo capacity for weapons that still fell short of purpose-built military standards. IncStar Dynamics' proposal, developed as the Ares Conventions were reshaping inter-state military agreements in the Inner Sphere, addressed both failings in a single purpose-built design.

Introduced in 2438, the Mk.I entered HAF service as the primary orbit-to-surface transport for armored and mechanized units and established the hull that would define the entire Ares lineage. IncStar Dynamics built the Mk.II Close Assault Landing Craft and the Mk.III Assault Craft on this same base frame, creating a three-branch family from one design. The Mk.I represented the long-range landing craft branch, the Mk.II became the close attack landing craft branch, and the Mk.III became the dedicated attack craft branch. All three entered service within thirteen years and operated together in mixed HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the early Star League period.

A lighter successor frame arrived in 2476 with the Mk.IV, ten tons lighter and slightly more maneuverable while retaining the same cargo and armor values. The Mk.V and Mk.VI carried the same lineage forward. These successor marks were themselves eventually replaced after the Star League's collapse by the Mark VII, which carried the long-range landing craft branch into the Succession Wars era under standard Inner Sphere technology. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War, having already dropped the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward in the fractured Inner Sphere.
